title: Technical Project Manager, Site Deployment, NA
description:
About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Position Overview

This role will be based in Sparks, Nevada & Pheonix, Arizona, following our flexible work policy (3 days in-office and 2 days flexible).

The Technical Project Manager, Site Deployment is responsible for managing the seamless transition of new data centers to Site Operations teams and ensuring Operational Readiness at Site Turnover from Construction. Requirements for this position include a strong understanding of data center facility operations, best practices, and site critical systems, combined with the ability to plan, track, and deliver multiple concurrent deployment projects on time and within defined operational quality standards.

This position is highly cross-functional, interfacing with peer teams in Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Business Operations, and Site Operations, requiring engagement at multiple levels of management throughout the company. This role demands both project management skill and technical acumen, as responsibilities include technical document reviews (e.g., Test and Balance (TAB) reports, commissioning documentation), verification of system performance, and ensuring operational standards are met prior to turnover.

This role is open on a rolling basis, and we review applications as they come in. There’s no set deadline, but if you’re interested, we encourage you to apply soon—our hiring needs can shift, and we welcome applications at any time while the opportunity is available.

Essential Job Functions

- Act as a key point of contact coordinating Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Business Operations, and Site Operations teams to seamlessly transition new data centers to Site Operations.

- Develop and manage detailed deployment project schedules, milestone tracking, and risk mitigation plans for site readiness activities.

- Perform technical reviews of commissioning documentation, TAB reports, and other turnover deliverables to validate operational performance and compliance with design intent.

- Manage the recruitment, staffing, onboarding, and training of new Operations teams at greenfield sites, contributing to the effective operational launch of these locations.

- Ensure complete program-level Operations protocols, procedures, and standards are in place for newly built facilities to achieve Operational Readiness.

- Ensure quality of Commissioning and Facility Acceptance necessary to deliver a technically sound facility to Site Operations.

Duties and Responsibilities

- Maintain communication and collaborate with stakeholders during all phases of a new data center build.

- Manage schedules and facilitate cross-team engagement keeping pace with Construction delivery dates.

- Track project deliverables against defined timelines and escalate risks/issues with recommended mitigation strategies.

- Ensure timely completion of Ops Site Deployment quality control checklists and Site Start-Up processes.

- Compile Procedures (MOP, SOP, EOP Templates) for Site Start Up across all Sites in deployment and adapt MOP, SOP, EOP templates to Site Specifics.

- Ensure the readiness of Operations Support spaces including Tool shop, Critical Spares storage spaces.

- Ensure the site is safe to operate with Safety Protocols, Safety Equipment, and Signage in place.

- Ensure Billing System Readiness and cross-functional contributions are fully coordinated.

- Ensure Asset Management Systems are in place and Site Equipment is fully accounted for including Warranty and Spare Parts information.

- Ensure CMMS is fully populated with equipment data and maintenance scheduling plans.

- Ensure the Site Security Systems are fully deployed at Site Turnover.

- Ensure Site Operators are fully trained and ready to operate and maintain critical systems.

- Ensure Permits, Licenses, Agreements are in place to facilitate Operations.

- Ensure 3rd party maintenance suppliers and contract agreements are set-up prior to Site Turnover.

- Support site mobilization including procuring spares, tools, and consumables.

- Lead formal technical review of O&M manuals, as-built & record drawings, permits, certificates, warranty documents, and commissioning reports prior to turnover.

- Perform site walks and site turnover walks to ensure Operational Readiness requirements are met.

- Share lessons learned that have been captured for consideration/mitigation in future builds.

- Coordinate and facilitate the formal transfer of site responsibility from Construction to Operations.

Job Requirements

- 3+ years of combined experience in data center or mission-critical project management and technical operations.

- Experience managing complex, cross-functional projects with defined schedules, budgets, and technical acceptance criteria.

- 2+ years of experience in a technical role in Critical Facilities Operations or Maintenance Operations with exposure to mechanical, electrical, and controls systems, OR

- 2+ years of experience in industrial Construction or Commissioning in a technical capacity, OR

- 2+ years of Project Management experience managing cross-functional or cross-team projects.

- Proficiency in interpreting and reviewing technical documents such as commissioning reports, TAB reports, electrical and mechanical drawings, and equipment submittals.

- Excellent time management and organizational skills and the ability to define these areas for other teams and team members.

- Ability to create teams from various departments and work in a high-level collaborative environment while promoting a teamwork mentality.

- Ability to initiate, drive, and deliver projects, and communicate plans and findings to internal customers and stakeholders.

- Project Management Professional (PMP) or similar certification preferred.

- Ability to travel up to 10% of total work time, including internationally in North America.

Physical Demands and Special Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to handle or feel objects; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs; balance; stoop or kneel; talk and hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.

Additional Details

This position is eligible for company benefits including but not limited to medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and AD&D, short and long-term disability coverage, paid time off, employee assistance, participation in a 401k program that includes company match, and many other additional voluntary benefits
Compensation for the role will depend on a number of factors, including your qualifications, skills, competencies, and experience and may fall outside of the range shown

We operate with No Ego and No Arrogance. We work to build each other up and support one another, appreciating each other’s strengths and respecting each other’s weaknesses. We find joy in our work and each other, actively seeking opportunities to inject fun into what we do. Our hard and efficient work is rewarded with an above market total compensation package. We offer a comprehensive suite of health and welfare, retirement, and paid leave benefits exceeding local expectations.

Throughout the year, the advantage of being part of the Vantage team is evident with an array of benefits, recognition, training and development, and the knowledge that your contribution adds value to the company and our community.

Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Accounting Department

Vantage Accounting Operations is a shared services team responsible for accurately and efficiently recording financial transactions while building positive financial relationships with customers and vendors across North America.

The team coordinates the entry, review, and approval of day-to-day transaction processing in accordance with financial policies and department SLA’s . The team members proactively engage in solving problems through close collaboration with internal and external partners in the development and implementation of continuous process improvements by enhancing the use of our technology resources, and continuing education to improve accounting operational efficiency through assessing, standardizing, and streamlining day-to-day processes. The team behaves with integrity, harmony, flexibility, respect, and initiative.

Position Overview

This role is based in Denver, Colorado with flexible work arrangement: 3 days on-site and 2 days remote.

Vantage seeks an experienced Accounts Payable Specialist to join the North American Shared Services team. This position analyzes and processes complex accounts payable transactions, partnering with internal and external stakeholders to research and resolve invoice discrepancies. Candidates should have strong quantitative and interpersonal skills, proficiency in A/P functions and software, and a collaborative mindset focused on building successful internal relationships. Adaptability and a willingness to learn are essential in our dynamic environment. Experience in real estate, construction, manufacturing, or production is preferred but not required.

This role operates with significant autonomy, managing large projects with limited oversight and engaging with senior-level managers or directors. The specialist handles complex challenges in invoice reconciliation, vendor relationships, and process optimization, while contributing to the development and implementation of new products, processes, standards, and operational plans that drive efficiency, accuracy, and strategic initiatives within the accounts payable function.

- Analyze accounts payable processes and recommend improvements to increase efficiency and reduce errors.

- Continuously monitor processes to ensure compliance and effectiveness.

- Maintain accurate and up-to-date accounts payable records.

- Assist with month-end and year-end closing processes, ensuring all invoices are accounted for.

- Prepare reports related to accounts payable activity, including aging reports and payment status updates.

- Degree in accounting or equivalent academic credentials preferred.

- 2–5 years of experience in Accounts Payable required.

- Strong knowledge of A/P processes and ability to manage a large volume of invoices.

- Understanding of accounting principles, including CAPEX and OPEX transactions.

- Experience in real estate, construction, or job cost accounting preferred but not required.

- Data center experience strongly preferred but not required.

- Ability to respond effectively to sensitive issues and complex inquiries.

- Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work with limited information.

- Detail-oriented with the ability to prioritize efficiently in a fast-paced environment.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) required; knowledge of Yardi Voyager and Certify preferred.

- Comfortable with IT systems and maintaining confidential records.

title: Physical Security Assurance Specialist, NA

description:
About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Physical Security Department
The North America Physical Security Department is focused on delivering a best-in-class security program aligned with Vantage’s vision of becoming the leading industry physical security data center provider. Our mission is to safeguard our data center environments through comprehensive, scalable, and standardized physical security processes that deter threats, promote rapid incident response, ensure regulatory compliance, and support Vantage’s rapid growth.
The department leads all physical security efforts across North America, ensuring that every Vantage data center operates within a consistent, scalable, and standardized security framework. Our teams design and implement physical security programs, systems, and processes that deter threats, strengthen site resiliency, and enable rapid response to incidents. We partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Construction, IT, and cross-functional stakeholders to ensure that physical security is embedded into every phase of the asset lifecycle and supports Vantage’s rapid expansion.

Position Overview
This role may be based at any Vantage location within the United States, following our flexible work policy (3 days in-office and 2 days flexible).

The Specialist, Physical Security Assurance and executes operational assurance, control-testing, assessment, and compliance activities supporting the North America Physical Security program. The Specialist evaluates whether physical security controls are appropriately implemented and operating effectively, documents defensible evidence and conclusions, identifies control deficiencies and risk themes, and coordinates corrective actions through validated closure.
Serving as a key connection between physical security standards and site-level execution, the Specialist applies consistent assurance methodologies across the portfolio and supports audit readiness, risk management, quality assurance, performance reporting, and continuous improvement. The role works cross-functionally with Security, Operations, Technology, Construction, and other stakeholders to strengthen control effectiveness, accountability, and program maturity.

Duties
Audit Execution and Control Testing

- Conduct site audits, assessments, and control testing across physical security environments

- Execute standardized control test procedures and validation processes aligned with enterprise frameworks

- Perform physical inspections of security infrastructure, including access control, video surveillance, and intrusion detection systems

- Validate system configuration, coverage, and operational performance

Data Collection and Documentation

- Collect, review, and maintain audit evidence in accordance with established standards and audit requirements

- Ensure all documentation is accurate, complete, and audit-ready

- Maintain detailed audit records, workpapers, and supporting artifacts

- Support development of audit reports and findings documentation

- Coordinate evidence collection and validation for internal and external audits, customer reviews, and other assurance activities

- Support document lifecycle activities, including version control, periodic review, approval tracking, publication, retention, and archival

Compliance Management

- Maintain the corrective-action register and monitor action owners, target dates, aging, status, and closure evidence

- Review remediation evidence to determine whether corrective actions sufficiently address identified deficiencies

- Escalate overdue, recurring, or material control deficiencies in accordance with established governance requirements

- Support root-cause analysis for recurring findings and systemic control weaknesses

- Support the maintenance of physical security risk registers and facilitate the linkage of assessment findings, control deficiencies, and corrective actions to applicable risks

Quality Assurance

- Conduct quality assurance reviews of physical security programs, processes, and audit deliverables to ensure consistency, accuracy, and alignment with established standards and governance requirements

- Analyze audit, assessment, and compliance data to identify trends, recurring control deficiencies, and opportunities for continuous improvement across the physical security program

- Support the development and maintenance of quality metrics, performance indicators, and assurance reporting to measure program effectiveness and drive operational excellence

- Maintain dashboards and recurring reports covering assessment completion, control-test results, findings by severity, remediation aging, overdue actions, repeat findings, evidence quality, and control effectiveness

Operational Assurance Support

- Perform periodic assurance checks and control reviews beyond formal audits

- Monitor and evaluate control performance and relevant system-health indicators

- Support the development and implementation of continuous-assurance processes and capabilities

- Manage assigned assessments and assurance deliverables with limited day-to-day supervision

Stakeholder Coordination

- Partner with site security teams, regional operations, and technical teams to clarify audit findings, validate corrective actions, and ensure alignment with security standards

- Provide clear, actionable feedback to stakeholders on required remediation actions

- Support cross-functional collaboration to improve control implementation and operational consistency

Job Requirements
Required

- Three or more years of relevant experience in physical security, quality assurance, audit, compliance, risk management, or a related control-based environment. Equivalent combinations of education, training, and experience may be considered

- Working knowledge of access control systems, video management systems, intrusion detection and alarm systems

- Ability to apply audit, assurance, quality-control, or control-testing methodologies and translate requirements into repeatable test procedures

- Experience developing dashboards and data visualizations using tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or similar platforms to track compliance, audit findings, corrective actions, and key performance indicators

- Strong attention to detail with the ability to collect, validate, and document evidence

- Ability to analyze and interpret control effectiveness and compliance requirements

- Experience documenting findings, managing corrective actions, reviewing remediation evidence, and monitoring issues through closure

- Strong written and verbal communication skills

- Ability to operate in a fast-paced, high-accountability environment

- Travel is expected up to 25%

Preferred

- Experience in data center, critical infrastructure, or enterprise environments

- Familiarity with governance frameworks, audit processes, or compliance programs

- Experience supporting SOC audits, customer audits, ISO-aligned management systems, or enterprise assurance programs

- Experience conducting physical security risk assessments, site-security reviews, or security vulnerability assessments

location_raw: Denver, Colorado; Ashburn, Virginia; Santa Clara, California; Sterling, Virginia; Remote - VA; Remote - IL; Remote - CO; Remote - CA
description:
About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.
Position Overview
This position can be based on-site at our office in Denver, CO, Ashburn, VA, Sterling, VA, Santa Clara, CA in alignment with our flexible work policy. (3 days on site required, 2 days flexible) or based remotely.

Vantage Data Centers is seeking a Principal Electrical Engineer to own all aspects of Electrical Engineering for our new age data center designs, ensuring that this discipline operates as an integrated part of the global product platform.
You will be accountable for the integrity, usability and evolution of standards, reference designs, approved variants and technical guidance across these areas. This includes defining where the platform must remain standard, where regional variation is appropriate, and how exceptions are governed when delivery realities require adaptation.

You will also own the mechanisms that connect design intent to project delivery across this discipline — including design governance, cross-discipline decision-making, readiness for handover, and the feedback loops that ensure field, commissioning and operational experience strengthens the next version of the platform.

Essential Job Functions
Energy storage and generation

- Lead integration of energy storage into data center electrical infrastructure to support resiliency, peak demand management, and operational flexibility

- Assess on-site generation solutions, including standby, prime power, and hybrid distributed systems, to support business, reliability, and sustainability goals

- Develop electrical strategies that integrate BESS, distributed generation, and advanced controls into mission-critical environments

- Provide technical leadership on interconnection, protection, and control philosophies for generation and energy storage assets

- Develop standards and design criteria for generation and energy storage topology, controls, safety, and commissioning

Product development

- Participate in the product development lifecycle from concept through implementation

- Work closely with Operations to balance cost-effective design solutions with long-term operational sustainability

- Develop and set minimum requirements for complete sequences of operation across designed systems

- Drive standards for electrical commissioning efforts

Design quality and delivery

- Review program-level design plans, equipment selections, and system submittals

- Ensure consistent execution through effective coordination and handoff to internal teams and external partners adapting the program prototype for site-specific use

- Work across engineering disciplines to deliver streamlined, practical solutions aligned with Operations and business needs

- Partner with regional product enablement teams to implement product intent consistently across projects and regions

- Support documentation handoff and coordination with regional teams and external consultants for site adaptation of global prototypes

Engineering analysis

- Apply engineering analysis tools and professional judgment to evaluate loads, lighting levels, and short-circuit currents

- Perform or guide the following studies:

- Load analysis and failure scenario calculations

- Short-circuit and overcurrent protection device coordination studies

- Arc flash mitigation studies

- Distribution analysis, including voltage drop and underground duct bank heat effect (Neher-McGrath) calculations

- Lighting photometric studies

Job Requirements

- Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering, or equivalent, from an accredited university or college

- Substantial experience in electrical power design and construction required, 10+ years preferred

- Data Center and/or mission critical experience is required

- Proficient in AutoCAD, Excel, Word, AmpCalc, ETAP, and PSCAD modeling software

- Working knowledge of critical power infrastructure within a data center

- Travel is expected to be 15–25% and may increase over time as business needs evolve.

Desired Qualifications

- Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering

- Professional license

- Experience in global, multi-region organizations operating with common standards and governed variants.

- Familiarity with industrialized delivery concepts such as evidence-based readiness, repeatable handover practices, and continuous improvement loops.

title: Manager, ServiceNow Platform Manager
description:
About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Position Overview
This role can be based in Denver, CO following our flexible work policy (3 days in-office, 2 days flexible). Or remote, US.

The Manager, ServiceNow Platform Owner is accountable for day-to-day platform prioritization, roadmap coordination, governance, readiness, supportability, and practical business value tracking for the ServiceNow platform. Reporting to the Platform Director, this role translates platform strategy into practical priorities, coordinates intake and delivery readiness, and ensures stakeholder commitments are visible, sequenced, and supportable.

The role may be consulted on adoption planning and adoption impacts but is not accountable for platform adoption. This position directly manages a ServiceNow Architect and ServiceNow Product Owner and works in close partnership with development, architecture, operations, security, SPM, PMO, finance, procurement, vendors, and business stakeholders; however, it does not directly oversee or manage the development team.

Essential Job Functions

Platform Governance & Standards

- Define practical standards for ServiceNow intake, prioritization, roadmap management, architecture review, release readiness, documentation, supportability, adoption input, and value tracking.

- Run ServiceNow governance routines and keep decisions, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, and escalations visible and traceable for the Platform Director and stakeholders.

- Continue maturing ServiceNow governance so it can act as a reusable standard for other enterprise platforms.

- Ensure ServiceNow functional boards are operational, decision-oriented, and supported by companion product owners who represent functional priorities.

- Reduce shadow work, unclear ownership, duplicate configuration, unmanaged customization, and unapproved commitments through clear ServiceNow guardrails.

Roadmap, Intake & Prioritization

- Maintain the ServiceNow roadmap, informed by business priorities, platform strategy, technical considerations, dependencies, risks, releases, and decisions.

- Ensure work enters through approved intake and is ready enough to sequence responsibly.

- Own ServiceNow platform content and communications channels, including the SharePoint site/web page, release notes, and bi-weekly platform updates; stakeholder and program updates remain PMO-owned.

- Manage ServiceNow platform prioritization and coordinate funding assumptions, delivery capacity inputs, architecture decisions, and risk tradeoffs with the Platform Director and partner teams.

Team Leadership

- Lead, coach, and develop the ServiceNow Architect and ServiceNow Product Owner, ensuring clear ownership for technical direction, product priorities, roadmap execution, stakeholder engagement, and platform outcomes.

- Set expectations for ServiceNow ownership, technical decision discipline, product management, communication, stakeholder management, governance participation, and measurable outcomes.

- Support hiring, role clarity, performance feedback, development planning, workload balance, and succession planning.

- Build an accountable ServiceNow team culture that balances speed, quality, platform health, business value, and sustainable operations.

Delivery Readiness & Risk Management

- Coordinate with development to ensure ServiceNow delivery commitments align to approved decisions, capacity inputs, architecture readiness, release timing, and support readiness.

- Set minimum readiness expectations for testing, documentation, support handoff, rollback planning, post-release ownership, and adoption-related inputs needed by business or change owners.

- Escalate risks affecting ServiceNow platform health, stakeholder commitments, budget, staffing, compliance, or enterprise outcomes.

- Serve as a consulted partner on ServiceNow platform health, technical debt, integration sprawl, customization risk, support complexity, data quality, and value realization where development or execution ownership sits with other teams.

Vendor, Metrics & Escalation Ownership

- Own large program statements of work with vendors, ensuring scope, deliverables, assumptions, dependencies, handoffs, and acceptance criteria are documented and aligned to ServiceNow platform priorities.

- Use metrics, usage insights, incident trends, backlog health, vendor performance inputs, and stakeholder feedback to inform prioritization recommendations, SOW adjustments, and resourcing discussions.

- Set day-to-day ServiceNow governance expectations, require decision traceability, return work that is not ready, manage platform prioritization within agreed guardrails, own large program vendor SOWs, and escalate priorities, risks, funding needs, staffing needs, or exceptions to the Platform Director.

Duties

- Partner with the Platform Director to translate ServiceNow strategy into an actionable platform roadmap.

- Coordinate intake, prioritization, governance, and readiness routines across ServiceNow stakeholders.

- Maintain clear visibility into platform commitments, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, and decisions.

- Partner with architecture, development, security, operations, finance, procurement, PMO, and business stakeholders to sequence work responsibly.

- Ensure ServiceNow communications, release notes, bi-weekly platform updates, and platform content are clear, current, and aligned to approved decisions.

- Lead the ServiceNow Architect and ServiceNow Product Owner through clear expectations, coaching, prioritization discipline, and role clarity.

- Support ServiceNow functional boards and companion product owners in representing business priorities and decision needs.

- Guide vendor SOW development and alignment to platform priorities, delivery assumptions, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.

- Monitor platform health indicators, backlog health, incident trends, stakeholder feedback, and adoption-related inputs to inform prioritization recommendations.

- Escalate risks, issues, resourcing needs, funding implications, or exceptions that impact ServiceNow platform outcomes.

title: Senior Product Operations Partner, Global
description:

Product Department

The Product team at Vantage defines and stewards our global product platform: the customer outcomes we aim to deliver, the standards and reference approaches that make delivery repeatable, and the closed-loop learning that turns each deployment into an upgrade for the next. We do this in partnership with Engineering, Delivery, Operations, Procurement, Sustainability, Sales, Site Selection, and Business Development, aligning priorities and trade-offs while preserving clear functional ownership for design execution, construction delivery, and site operations.

Position Overview

This role is based in Denver, CO in alignment with our flexible work policy. (3 days on site required, 2 days flexible).

Product Operations builds the operating system that enables the Product organization to make better decisions, scale knowledge, adopt new ways of working, and execute predictably. This role is a hands-on builder and organizational multiplier who improves the mechanisms behind that system.

The Senior Product Operations Partner, Global for Systems & Enablement connects patterns across teams, turns recurring friction into practical improvements, and builds solutions that make work clearer, faster, and easier to sustain. The role does not stop at identifying opportunities or recommending changes. It tests ideas, implements solutions, gathers feedback, and iterates until better ways of working become durable operating practices.

This role will initially own practical activities such as forum operations, document publishing, library administration, onboarding resources, and technology enablement. Success means continuously improving and automating these mechanisms so the role—and the organization’s capacity—evolves significantly over time. The responsibilities should look meaningfully different after the first 12 months because repetitive administrative work has been simplified, automated, or redesigned.

This is a highly autonomous individual contributor role for someone who can move between coordination and creation, influence without formal authority, and use AI and automation as practical tools today. The role strengthens the systems around accountable owners and trio roles without taking over their delivery responsibilities.

Essential Job Functions

You will own and improve the enablement mechanisms that make the Product organization easier to operate, scale, and navigate. This includes operating-rhythm execution, governance workflows, document publishing, digital workplace patterns, onboarding resources , and AI-enabled process improvements.

You will be expected to:

- Carry essential operational work while actively redesigning how it is completed.

- Connect common needs and pain points across teams instead of solving each request in isolation.

- Build, test, launch, and improve practical solutions—not only prepare recommendations.

- Reduce manual effort and administrative burden through clearer workflows, reusable tools, automation, and self-service resources.

- Increase the organization’s capacity by making important information, processes, and decisions easier to access and act on.

- Regularly reassess the role’s recurring responsibilities, reducing manual administration and shifting capacity toward higher-leverage enablement, automation, and organizational improvement.

Document Publishing and Library Administration

- Own the operational coordination of document releases, including validating handoffs, tracking readiness, and moving approved files into the appropriate library locations.

- Apply and validate document metadata, file naming, versioning, ownership, permissions, and library placement in partnership with document owners.

- Keep downstream application rules, mappings, and release records aligned with published document changes.

- Complete post-publishing checks and update release tracking to confirm accuracy and completion.

- Improve the publishing process by reducing manual handoffs, strengthening quality controls, and introducing automation where practical.

- Build clear instructions, templates, and self-service resources so routine publishing activities become easier for document owners to complete correctly.

- Identify patterns in publishing issues and implement changes that prevent repeat errors.

Operating Rhythm, Forums, and Follow-Through

- Own the operational setup and ongoing effectiveness of assigned Product leadership forums, governance routines, councils, and operating reviews.

- Establish clear inputs, deadlines, agendas, outputs, decision records, and follow-through mechanisms for each forum.

- Maintain the Product operating calendar and improve how related forums connect, sequence, and share information.

- Create practical mechanisms for accountable owners to surface progress, decisions, risks, and dependencies without introducing unnecessary reporting burden.

- Identify recurring coordination work that can be standardized, delegated, automated, or eliminated.

- Improve the forum experience over time so meeting administration decreases while decision quality, visibility, and accountability increase.

Workflow Improvement, AI, and Automation

- Identify high-friction or repetitive Product Operations workflows and determine whether they should be simplified, automated, consolidated, or retired.

- Build and test practical AI-enabled workflows, prompts, templates, agents, automations, and knowledge-retrieval patterns.

- Use Microsoft 365, Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate, SharePoint, Teams, Loop, Planner, or equivalent tools to reduce manual effort and improve information flow.

- Move beyond proof of concept by documenting, launching, monitoring, and iterating solutions with the people who use them.

- Connect similar needs across teams and create reusable solutions that address multiple pain points at once.

- Partner with functional owners and technology teams to move successful experiments into secure, maintainable operating practices.

- Track the time saved, friction reduced, adoption achieved, or decision quality improved through implemented changes.

Communications and Organizational Visibility

- Translate leadership direction, decisions, and operating changes into concise, audience-appropriate communications and practical next steps.

- Build repeatable mechanisms that keep teams informed without relying on unnecessary meetings.

- Test and implement new communication approaches, such as automated updates, digest-style communications, resource hubs, or targeted distribution patterns.

- Connect information across functions and surface themes, dependencies, or recurring questions that may otherwise remain fragmented.

- Measure the usefulness of communication mechanisms and refine them based on feedback and engagement.

Team Onboarding and Enablement Experience

- Own and continuously improve the Product-specific onboarding experience in support of the People & Culture onboarding journey and the Product Transformation & Integration onboarding roadmap.

- Maintain current, easy-to-navigate onboarding materials, resource paths, team context, tool guidance, and operating-model references.

- Build reusable onboarding journeys that help new hires and internal transfers understand how the Product organization works and where to find support.

- Partner with hiring managers and People teams so Product onboarding complements, rather than replaces, manager-owned launch plans.

- Gather onboarding feedback, identify patterns, and implement improvements that close knowledge gaps and reduce reliance on one-to-one explanations.

- Introduce automation and self-service where it improves consistency without making the experience impersonal.

Additional duties as assigned by management.

Job Requirements

- Demonstrated experience improving how a team or organization works—not only coordinating existing processes.

- A track record of taking ambiguous problems from observation through implementation, adoption, and iteration.

- Hands-on experience applying AI, automation, workflow, or productivity tools to real business processes in ways that reduce effort or improve outcomes.

- Familiarity with Power Automate, Copilot, Copilot Studio, SharePoint, Teams, or equivalent tools preferred.

- Strong systems thinking and pattern recognition, with the ability to connect needs across teams and design reusable solutions.

- Ability to balance practical execution with critical thinking about whether a task, process, meeting, or workflow should operate differently.

- Experience supporting senior leaders or leadership teams by turning direction into clear communications, operating mechanisms, and follow-through.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce concise, audience-appropriate messages and resources.

This role will be based in Denver, CO. Following our flexible work policy (3 days in-office, 2 days flexible).
The Senior Data Governance Manager, Operations NA enables North America Operations to use data confidently and consistently to manage performance, identify risk, prioritize action, and improve operational outcomes. This individual contributor establishes and operationalizes the governance practices needed to ensure structured and unstructured Operations data is clearly defined, appropriately owned, reliable, traceable, and fit for purpose.

The role works directly with Operations leaders, functions, data owners, and stewards to clarify accountability, standardize critical data and metric definitions, resolve quality issues, and embed governance into everyday business processes. It translates enterprise data standards into practical approaches that improve data trust and usability without creating unnecessary complexity for Operations.

The role serves as a connective point across Operations, Operations Data & Intelligence, Global Data & AI, and technology teams, establishing feedback loops that translate operational needs, data issues, and user feedback into   improvements to data definitions, controls, products, and source systems. The ideal candidate combines strong data-governance expertise with hands-on execution, business partnership, and the ability to drive cross-functional accountability and continuous improvement.

- Develop and maintain the Operations data-governance framework, roadmap, decision rights, and operating practices in alignment with enterprise standards.

- Facilitate governance decisions and drive resolution of cross-functional data ownership, definition, quality, access, and usage issues.

title: Critical Support Specialist, NA --Electrical/Generators
description:
About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Effective 9.8.26 the CSS role will be adjusted from Chiller CSS to Electrical CSS with a emphasis on generator expert.

Site Operations Department

The Site Operations Department is responsible for the overall health of all mechanical and electrical systems, building maintenance, and performance of all data modules in our data centers. The team is staffed 24 x 7 onsite with Critical Facility Engineers (CFEs) on each shift.

This team is the face of Vantage to our customers and the first line of defense regarding the uptime of our campus as well as the performance of our customer installations. Using a Critical Maintenance Management System (CMMS) to plan and track work needed, the Site Operations department performs all preventative and corrective maintenance. Our culture expects and rewards team performance that engages directly with the customers and the facility infrastructure. This is a team that does most of the actual work versus calling upon vendors. As a result, we provide superior service that is faster and more cost effective.

Position Overview

Critical Support Specialist roles are SMEs (Subject Matter Experts) and highly-trained in specific areas within the data center electrical/mechanical space. See specialization list below.

This particular CSS is available for a talented Hands-on Generator / Electrical to be a Subject Matter Expert for our Virginia campuses. This role will be working onsite Monday - Friday day shift in Sterling/Ashburn, VA. This role additionally will travel 15-20% in North America, mostly in the United States data center campuses. The person in this role should expect to do at least 4 sites visits a year to do operational technical assessment and will also travel for complex repairs on equipment specific issues.

We are looking for a Critical Support Specialist who knows what best-in-class service looks like and can make that a reality. This role is a crucial member of our facilities team, managing some of the most efficient and cost-effective data center facilities in the industry. The successful candidate for this role will work with a team of other electrical and mechanical-focused engineers performing maintenance and repair for our data center infrastructure. We take our customer requirements for uptime seriously and keep our facilities maintained to a very high standard to ensure uninterrupted service for our customers.

If you enjoy working on critical data center systems (UPSs, PDUs, Diesel Generators, ATS equipment and Building Controls), as well as industrial electrical equipment and systems that include power distribution components/wiring, electronic components, and lighting systems, know the importance of getting it right the first time and not disrupting mission critical data centers, and enjoy delighting customers with superior service, then please read on!

Essential Job Functions

- Perform detailed, specialized maintenance, troubleshooting, and operational tasks within your area of expertise, ensuring uninterrupted data center operations.

- Independently manage complex maintenance projects and system enhancements with minimal supervision.

- Respond effectively to safety incidents and emergency situations, maintaining a secure work environment.

- Exercise discretion and judgment in adapting workflows to shifting priorities.

- Collaborate frequently with internal teams across multiple organizational levels and externally with vendors and technical partners.

- Additional duties as assigned by Management.

Duties by Specialization: -- this particular role will be for Electrical/Generator Engineer

Low Voltage Electrical Specialist:

- Operate, maintain, and repair critical low voltage electrical infrastructure including substations, utility switchgear, transformers, feeders and distribution systems, power metering, power generators, automatic transfer switches (ATS), uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), batteries, power distribution units (PDUs), static transfer switches (STSs), remote power panels (RPPs), and associated controls.

- Conduct comprehensive inspections and preventive maintenance, implementing detailed solutions to enhance reliability and operational effectiveness.

- Act as a subject matter expert in low voltage electrical systems, providing detailed technical guidance, training, and mentoring junior team members.

- Lead complex troubleshooting efforts, document findings, and contribute significantly to procedural documentation and training materials.

Medium Voltage Electrical Specialist:

- Manage and maintain medium voltage electrical systems such as substations, utility switchgear, transformers, feeders and distribution systems, and protection and control circuitry.

- Oversee preventive maintenance schedules, detailed system inspections, and extensive repairs, ensuring strict compliance with regulatory and safety standards.

- Act as a technical leader, providing detailed expert-level troubleshooting, resolution of complex electrical issues, and mentoring junior personnel.

- Document comprehensive technical procedures and collaborate with engineering teams on system enhancements and updates.

UPS Systems Specialist:

- Perform detailed preventive and corrective maintenance tasks, including major component replacements and complete system recalibrations.

- Independently manage critical UPS system maintenance schedules, ensuring tasks are prioritized effectively.

- Independently apply advanced troubleshooting skills to identify and rectify intricate UPS issues, such as rectifier or inverter failures.

- Collaborate closely with engineering teams on detailed UPS system upgrades, modifications, or enhancements based on operational requirements.

- Provide technical insights and recommendations for improving UPS efficiency, reliability, and overall system performance.

Generator Specialist:

- Perform comprehensive maintenance and operational tasks for generator electrical and mechanical systems, including routine and corrective maintenance.

- Provide technical leadership and oversight for generator operations and maintenance, including the development and implementation of preventive maintenance schedules and strategies.

- Serve as the lead technical expert on major generator projects, planning and executing system upgrades and maintenance initiatives.

- Ensure strict compliance with industry regulations, codes, and standards related to generator operations, contributing to regulatory audits and adherence to safety and environmental protocols.

- Act as a mentor and trainer, imparting expert knowledge to junior technicians and other staff.

HVAC Systems Specialist:

- Oversee comprehensive operations and detailed maintenance of critical HVAC infrastructure systems, including chilled water and condenser water systems, computer room air handlers (CRAH), computer room air conditioners (CRAC), humidity control systems, leak detection, commercial AC systems, constant and variable airflow systems, boilers, and air compressors.

This team is the face of Vantage to our customers and the first line of defense regarding the uptime of our campus as well as the performance of our customer installations. Using a Critical Maintenance Management System (CMMS) to plan and track work needed, the Site Operations department performs all preventative and corrective maintenance. Our culture expects and rewards team performance that engages directly with the customers and the facility infrastructure. This is a team that does most of the actual work versus calling upon vendors. As a result, we provide superior service that is faster and more cost effective.

Position Overview
Critical Support Specialist roles are SMEs (Subject Matter Experts) and highly-trained in specific areas within the data center electrical/mechanical space. See specialization list below.

This particular CSS is available for a Hands-on Chiller Tech-Engineer / Commercial-Industrial HVAC to be a Subject Matter Expert for our Santa-Clara, CA or Reno, NV campuses.
This role will be working onsite Monday - Friday day shift. This role additionally will travel 15-20% in North America, mostly in the United States data center campuses.

We are looking for a Critical Support Specialist who knows what best-in-class service looks like and can make that a reality. This role is a crucial member of our facilities team, managing some of the most efficient and cost-effective data center facilities in the industry. The successful candidate for this role will work with a team of other electrical and mechanical-focused engineers performing maintenance and repair for our data center infrastructure. We take our customer requirements for uptime seriously and keep our facilities maintained to a very high standard to ensure uninterrupted service for our customers.

This role is responsible for developing a comprehensive global benefits strategy that aligns with Vantage's business objectives, supports our employees' well-being, and enables our continued international growth.

The Director will lead benefits strategy and operations across North America, EMEA and APAC, ensuring compliance with local regulations, driving operational excellence, optimizing vendor partnerships, and delivering a consistent employee experience globally while balancing regional market needs. This role will partner closely with People & Culture, Payroll, Finance, Legal, and external providers to ensure our programs remain competitive, sustainable, and scalable.

The Director will establish and continuously evolve Vantage's global benefits philosophy, balancing employee wellbeing, market competitiveness, financial stewardship, and regional flexibility. This leader will leverage data, technology, and market intelligence to build scalable programs that enhance employee experience while supporting Vantage's long-term business strategy.

Essential Duties

Global Benefits Strategy and Design

- Develop and execute a comprehensive global benefits strategy that supports Vantage's growth objectives, talent strategy, and employee value proposition.

- Establish and continuously evolve Vantage's global benefits philosophy, balancing employee wellbeing, market competitiveness, fiscal responsibility, and regional flexibility.

- Lead the evaluation, design, and enhancement of health, welfare, retirement, wellbeing, leave, and ancillary benefit programs globally.

- Lead the evolution of Vantage's global wellbeing strategy, including physical, mental, financial, and family wellbeing programs that strengthen employee engagement, productivity, and retention.

- Ensure benefits programs remain competitive through regular market benchmarking and analysis of industry best practices.

- Establish governance frameworks that balance global consistency with regional flexibility and local market requirements.

Benefits Operations and Administration

- Oversee the administration and delivery of all global benefits programs, ensuring operational excellence, scalability, and a high-quality employee experience.

- Drive the optimization of benefits technology, self-service capabilities, and digital employee experiences through Workday and other global benefits administration platforms.

- Continuously evaluate and implement technology solutions that simplify administration, improve data quality, and enhance the overall employee experience.

- Develop and maintain standardized processes, controls, and documentation to ensure efficient and compliant program administration.

- Partner with internal stakeholders and external vendors to ensure accurate enrollment, eligibility management, claims administration, and employee support.

Vendor and Consultant Management

- Lead the selection, negotiation, and management of global benefits brokers, consultants, administrators, and other service providers.

- Develop long-term strategic partnerships with global vendors to drive innovation, improve service delivery, and maximize return on investment.

- Drive vendor performance through established service-level agreements, performance metrics, audits, and regular business reviews.

- Identify opportunities for program enhancements, consolidation, and cost optimization through vendor partnerships.

Compliance and Risk Management

- Ensure compliance with all applicable regulations and reporting requirements across jurisdictions, including health and welfare plans, retirement plans, leave programs, and applicable tax regulations.

title: Vice President, Global HR Technology & People Platforms, Global
description:
About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Position Overview
This role can be based in Denver, CO following our flexible work policy (3 days in-office, 2 days flexible), or remote, US.

The VP, Global HR Technology & People Platforms is the enterprise product owner for Vantage’s People technology ecosystem, responsible for transforming Workday and a new HR Service Delivery Platform into a scalable, intelligent operating system for workforce planning, talent deployment, and employee experience.
Reporting to the Chief People Officer, this role will define and execute the strategy to:

- Embed end-to-end people processes into Workday (planning → hiring → development → mobility → promotion → backfill)

- Stand up a new HR Service Delivery Platform as the global service delivery layer

- Enable a closed-loop talent flywheel that prioritizes internal mobility, improves workforce productivity, and links talent decisions to business demand

This leader will operate as a product executive, not just a systems owner, driving process standardization, automation, data governance, and AI enablement across HR, Finance and IT to delivery measurable business outcomes.

Core Accountabilities
1 . Platform Strategy & Product Ownership

- Own the global People Technology strategy and roadmap across Workday, HR Service Delivery platform, and adjacent systems

- Position: Workday as the system of execution for workforce and talent decisions and HR Service Delivery platform as the employee service and experience layer

- Ensure platforms are designed as connected products, not siloed tools

2. End-to-End People Process Architecture (Core of the Role)

- Design and implement integrated, end-to-end people workflows, including:
workforce planning → requisition → hiring → mobility → promotion → backfill

- Translate workforce demand (Adaptive planning) into approved roles, hiring actions and internal mobility opportunities

- Embed decision logic and automation, including internal vs external hiring (“build vs buy”), promotion and lateral movement rules and compensation triggers aligned to job architecture

- Drive global standardization of people processes

3. Talent Flywheel & Internal Mobility Engine

- Build and operationalize a closed-loop talent flywheel: demand → match → move → backfill → repeat

- Leverage: performance data, succession plans, skills taxonomy

- Enable internal-first hiring and talent deployment strategies

- Ensure seamless orchestration of recruiting, succession, promotions and workforce planning

4. HR Service Delivery & Employee Experience Layer

- Implement and scale a global HR Service Delivery platform

- Define and optimize service catalog & case taxonomy, knowledge management, employee and manager self-service

- Drive AI-enabled service delivery (case deflection, virtual agents)

- Align service delivery to shared services operating model

5. Data, Architecture & Enabling Foundations

- Ensure foundational capabilities are designed and embedded: job architecture (job families, levels), taxonomy and mapping skills, compensation structures and bands, career pathways (as needed)

- Enable these to support: workforce planning, talent matching, compensation decisions

6. AI, Automation & Innovation

- Identify and deploy AI-enabled capabilities, including talent matching and recommendations, service automation and case resolution

- Ensure responsible AI governance, data privacy, and compliance

- Drive measurable productivity and efficiency gains

7. Execution, Delivery & Scale

- Own global HR technology delivery: releases, integrations, enhancements

- Lead multi-region transformation programs

- Ensure platforms scale with business growth and complexity

Job Requirements

- 10–15+ years of progressive experience in HRIS, HR Technology, or People Systems leadership roles

- Familiarity with AI-enabled HR technologies and experience integrating automation, intelligent workflows, or emerging AI capabilities into business processes while maintaining appropriate governance and data privacy standards.

- Deep, hands-on expertise with Workday HCM, including configuration, reporting, and module integration

- Proven experience leading HRIS teams in complex, multi-site, or global organizations

- Strong understanding of HR processes across core HR, compensation, benefits, talent, and payroll integrations

- Experience managing large-scale system implementations, upgrades, or transformations

- Strong stakeholder management skills across HR, IT, Finance, and executive leadership

- Demonstrated ability to translate business needs into scalable system solutions

- Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in HR, Information Systems, or related field preferred

- Experience with data governance, HR compliance, and systems controls

Preferred

- Experience with advanced Workday capabilities (e.g., Advanced Reporting, Security, Integrations)

- Experience deploying or scaling AI-enabled capabilities within Workday or the broader HR technology ecosystem.

- Familiarity with generative AI, agentic workflows, and emerging technologies supporting employee experience, service delivery, and workforce analytics.

- HR Shared Services and Service Delivery Platform experience

- Experience in high-growth or rapidly scaling organizations

- Strong HR analytics / people data experience

- Experience leading cross-functional transformation (HR + IT + Finance)

- Change management and stakeholder communication expertise

Why This Matters
HR technology is a critical lever for growth, not just an operational support function. It determines whether the organization can deploy talent against business demand with speed, precision, and consistency at scale.
This role ensures our platforms evolve into an integrated system of execution—providing trusted data, enabling automation, and embedding decision logic directly into our people processes. The outcome is a more agile organization where hiring, movement, and workforce decisions are faster, smarter, and more aligned to business priorities, while delivering consistent and scalable employee experience globally.
HRIS is a foundational enabler of scale, efficiency, and workforce visibility. It determines whether the organization can effectively hire, manage, and pay talent at speed and at scale. description:
About Vantage

Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Market Development Department
The Market Development (MD) team is responsible for 4 key functions within the North American business: 1) Market Strategy, 2) Site Selection & Acquisition, 3) New Site Development and 4) Preconstruction. The team drives the business plans and execution of our geographic and vertical market expansions across North America. We are at the front-end of the process of ensuring we have the critical capacity required to meet the evolving requirements of our wholesale and hyperscale customer base. We evaluate supply, demand, pricing, network, power, and a myriad of other factors when developing our market and site plans. We then acquire sites that align with those plans. The team collaborates with Commercial Management, Sales, Solution Engineering, Design Engineering, Construction, Operations, Finance, and Senior Management along the way. We also help ensure optimal revenue realization post-construction through development of commercial constructs and pricing that aligns to the objectives of both Vantage and our customers.

Position Overview
This role can be based in any of our US locations: Denver, CO; Phoenix, AZ; San Antonio, TX, Santa Clara, CA;  Columbus; Ohio, Atlanta; Georgia; Ashburn, VA, or US Remote.
Vantage is looking for a meticulous, hands-on Preconstruction Manager to support future project deployments and participate in regional programmatic initiatives with a focus on pre-construction estimating, development delivery, scheduling, and cost optimization. You will join the Preconstruction team in providing professional cost, schedule, risk, and constructability analysis for perspective developments guiding business level decisions on regional capital expenditure across North America. This role provides a unique opportunity to provide immediate feedback on cost drivers ranging from unique site characteristics, construction strategy, building design, to cost savings opportunities. Preconstruction Managers will also be responsible for generating site specific CapEx proformas, conceptual estimating, reviewing general contractor RFPs, coordinating new site delivery schedules, and evaluating strategic construction elements on perspective new sites.

Essential Job Functions

- Lead the generation of Capital Expenditure Proformas associated with New Site Developments across Vantages portfolio. Serving in partnership with New Site Development, you will be on the forefront co-leading project development strategy, business cases, and forecasting revenue ready dates

- Create cost studies at all levels of project development, with heavy focus on conceptual planning and pre-construction phases. This role will partner with the New Site Development (NSD), Construction (CON), Design Management (DM), Design Engineering (DE), Procurement, Power, and Site Selection/Market Development (MKTDEV) teams to ensuring that project cost is accurately accounted for.

- Maintain and develop company processes and procedures around our internal project development cost data base to guide future CapEx development decisions.

- Prepare independent internal take-offs, cost estimates, and cash flow/commitment ledgers from conceptual ideas and plans to Construction Document sets.

- Coordinate with internal customers to surface cost and schedule risk associate with perspective projects.

- Serve as a subject matter expert to internal stakeholders on construction and development cost across North American Markets. Challenge internal and external data and ensure justification for modifications, inclusions, or exclusions of presented costs to VDC Preconstruction.

- Review complex General Contractor and Major Trade proposals for new projects, assisting local project teams with evaluating cost, scope and schedule impacts of proposals.

- Ensure all project work scope has been included in the project estimates; verify all scope, durations, and assumptions included in each estimate and supports the authorization and release of internal budgets and estimates.

- Work with vertical peers focusing on continuous improvement to our business processes.

- Analyze drawings, specifications, proposals, and other documentation to prepare/review/comment on time, cost, and labor estimates for projects.

- Review quantity take-off as a separate validation of contractor pricing in a manner and level of detail consistent with the project goals.

- Review and implement lessons learned to ensure estimating data is accurate and competitive.

- Understand and handle competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

- Develop and maintain relationships with subcontractors / partners.

- Research new products and installation techniques and develop cost roadmaps to ensure competitive pricing related to sustainability, data center design, and other Vantage initiatives.

Job Requirements

- Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Quantity Estimating, Accounting, Finance, Economics or relevant functional discipline or equivalent combination of education and experience

- 8 years of related experience

- Experience leading new construction budgeting and pricing efforts for all trade disciplines

- Data Center or MEP estimating experience is strongly preferred

- Project level green and brown field new construction experience is strongly preferred

- Knowledge of all engineering scopes, including electrical, mechanical, structural, and civil

- Expert knowledge and experience of technical processes, engineering standards, state, and federal codes, analyzing data, generating reports for internal and external review and comment

- Demonstrated knowledge of and experience using cost/estimating software

- Experience preparing/reviewing contingency evaluation, durations, escalation, reconciliations for estimates

- Ability to interpret construction plans, drawings, sketches, and specifications

- Familiarity with ProCore & Power BI

- Extensive experience using Microsoft Office software tools, such as MS Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and Word, to be utilized in managing and reporting estimate throughput, status, and labor allocation

- Travel required is expected to be up to 25% but may increase over time as the business evolves

Additional Details

- Salary Range: $165,000 - $175,000 Base + Bonus (this range is based for Colorado on market data and may vary in other locations)

- This position is eligible for company benefits including but not limited to medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and AD&D, short and long-term disability coverage, paid time off, employee assistance, participation in a 401k program that includes company match, and many other additional voluntary benefits.

title: Cybersecurity AI Risk and Governance Director, Global
description:
About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Cybersecurity Department
The AI Cybersecurity Director is responsible for the technical security, risk management, and governance enforcement of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and large language model (LLM) systems deployed across Vantage's operational, OT, and enterprise environments.

This role serves as the technical and security authority for AI security, ensuring AI systems are architected, deployed, and operated with appropriate controls for data protection, model integrity, access governance, monitoring, and human‑in‑the‑loop decision enforcement. The AI Cybersecurity Director ensures AI technologies deliver business value without introducing unacceptable cyber, operational, safety, workforce, or regulatory risk, in alignment with the Global Policies and Standards.

This role is based in Denver, CO or Ashburn, VA. In alignment with our flexible work policy (3 days on site required, 2 days flexible).

Essential Functions

- Establish enterprise governance for detection, classification, and management of unauthorized (shadow) AI across business units, in coordination with centralized AI functions.

- Define and enforce security architecture standards for AI, ML, and LLM platforms across cloud, hybrid, on‑prem, and OT‑adjacent environments.

- Provide security design oversight and approval for AI systems, including data pipelines, model hosting, inference paths, APIs, and integrations.

- Define enterprise methodology for AI security assessment covering architecture, design, and implementation across applications, agents, and workflows.

- Ensure AI architectures enforce segmentation, least privilege, deterministic behavior, and fail‑safe operation, particularly where OT or critical infrastructure data is involved.

- Establish AI‑specific incident response playbooks and lead response to AI‑related security, safety, or governance incidents.

- Enforce controls preventing unauthorized model retraining, autonomous learning, or use of live production or OT data outside approved intent.

- Define security requirements for explainability, traceability, and output validation where AI influences operational, workforce, safety, or compliance outcomes.

- Drive alignment with ISO 42001 and related AI governance standards across applicable teams.

AI Data Protection and Trust Boundaries

- Enforce protections against prompt injection, data leakage, hallucination risk, unauthorized context expansion, and external model training exposure.

- Ensure sensitive enterprise, operational, personnel, and contractual data is not exposed to or retained by external AI platforms without approved safeguards.

- Approve and oversee AI data ingestion pipelines, enforcing purpose limitation, data minimization, and classification requirements.

- Validate encryption, access logging, retention, and deletion controls for data used by AI systems.

- Define and enforce controls preventing cross‑domain data correlation that violates trust boundaries or governance constraints.

AI Threat, Risk, and Monitoring Management

- Perform AI‑specific threat modeling, including risks such as data poisoning, model theft, inference abuse, output manipulation, and decision integrity compromise.

- Integrate AI threats into enterprise cybersecurity and OT risk models, including definition of compensating controls and escalation for systems exceeding risk tolerance.

- Own and maintain the AI risk register covering confidentiality, integrity, availability, explainability, data quality, model drift, adversarial attacks, and business impact.

- Ensure AI systems generate telemetry, logging, and audit trails sufficient to detect misuse, drift, or anomalous behavior.

- Integrate AI security monitoring into SOC, SIEM, and enterprise incident response workflows.

OT and Critical Infrastructure Safeguards

- Enforce prohibitions on autonomous AI control of OT assets, including power, cooling, BMS, fire suppression, and physical access systems.

- Validate one‑way data flows, read‑only access models, and manual override requirements where AI consumes OT telemetry.

- Partner with OT and infrastructure teams to ensure AI enhances visibility and decision support without compromising safety, reliability, or uptime.

- Oversee security reviews of vendor‑provided and embedded AI capabilities, including model behavior, data handling, and contractual protections.

- Define and enforce minimum security and governance requirements for AI vendors, including audit rights and termination conditions.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience.

- Minimum 10+ years of experience in cybersecurity, security architecture, or risk engineering roles.

- Hands‑on experience securing data pipelines, APIs, cloud platforms, and analytics or ML‑enabled systems.

- Strong understanding of identity, access management, encryption, logging, and secure system design.

Preferred Qualifications

- Direct experience securing AI/ML platforms, LLMs, or analytics pipelines.

- Experience with cloud security (Azure, AWS, GCP) and SaaS‑based AI platforms.

- Familiarity with OT, critical infrastructure, or safety‑critical environments.

- Security certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, CISM, or cloud security certifications.

Key Skills & Competencies

- AI and machine learning security

- LLM and generative AI risk management

- Security architecture and threat modeling

- Data protection and access governance

- Incident response and forensic analysis

- Cross‑functional technical leadership

The ability to   acquire , integrate,   optimize , and scale energy infrastructure has become a strategic differentiator.

The Senior Director, Energy Systems   is responsible for   defining and stewarding Vantage’s global energy systems strategy and product roadmap.

This role owns the vision, strategy, and development of the energy layer of the Vantage product platform, translating evolving utility markets, interconnection and regulatory changes, customer requirements, power infrastructure constraints, grid modernization trends, and validated technology innovations into scalable energy products and deployment models.

The position serves as the primary product steward for Vantage’s energy systems portfolio, including behind-, front-, across-the-meter energy solutions, power generation integration, energy storage, grid-interactive infrastructure, energy optimization systems, and future energy platform capabilities.

Success in this role requires a demonstrated blend of commercial, technical, and strategic   expertise . The ideal candidate possesses deep knowledge of energy markets, energy contracting and partnerships, utility interconnection processes, many power generation technologies, transmission and distribution systems, and energy infrastructure development, while also understanding how to convert those capabilities into repeatable product offerings that create long-term competitive advantage. First-hand experience is preferred, especially across multiple regions (e.g., utilities / balancing authorities, ISOs / RTOs), types of energy partners (e.g., OEMs, EPCs, IPPs), and partnership methods (e.g., JV, equity, co-development).

Working closely with teams across the Energy and Product   organizations   this individual will ensure energy innovations evolve into scalable platform capabilities that can be consistently deployed across Vantage’s global footprint.

Role Purpose

The role   establishes   how energy infrastructure, generation resources, storage systems, utility relationships, grid integration strategies, and emerging energy solutions contribute to customer value, capacity growth, resilience, speed-to-market, and long-term business performance.

The Senior Director, Energy Systems owns the integration of those validated technologies into the product roadmap, platform architecture, deployment strategies, and regional enablement models.

The role also serves as a bridge between innovation and scale — ensuring that evolving energy capabilities move beyond successful pilots and become durable, repeatable, globally deployable product offerings while also communicating energy needs back to inform the next generation of innovation.

Global Energy Strategy

- Develop multi-year roadmaps for energy infrastructure, power acquisition strategies, generation integration, storage deployment, and grid-connected energy solutions.

- Translate customer requirements, market intelligence, supply chain constraints, utility dynamics, interconnection evolution, regulatory changes, and policy developments into product direction and investment priorities.

- Evaluate future energy trends and   determine   where Vantage should build, buy, partner, or influence.

- Develop executive-level strategic recommendations and investment cases for energy-related initiatives.

Energy Systems Product Portfolio

- Own the product strategy and portfolio for energy-related platform capabilities.

- Define repeatable energy system architectures, deployment models, standards, and intentional variants.

- Establish energy product requirements and roadmap priorities aligned to Vantage’s regional and customer growth strategies.

- Create scalable approaches for: power generation integration, energy storage systems, grid-interactive infrastructure, load flexibility and energy optimization, utility coordination frameworks, and energy management and control systems.

- Ensure energy capabilities are developed as reusable platform components rather than project-specific solutions.

Utility, Interconnection & Power Market Leadership
