- Proactively translate evolving grid requirements into the energy platform.

- Develop frameworks and guidance related   to:   utility partnerships, grid interconnection strategy, capacity acquisition approaches, transmission and distribution considerations, and power market participation opportunities.

- Support strategic customer opportunities requiring sophisticated energy solutions.

- Evaluate regional power market dynamics and their implications for platform strategy.

Road mapping  & Technology Integration

- Partner closely with the Senior Director, Advanced Technologies to incorporate validated innovations into the Vantage product roadmap and provide evolving energy needs to inform the next generation of innovation.

- Translate technology pilot outcomes and validation results into product requirements, deployment standards, and investment priorities.

- Collaborate with Product Engineering to ensure roadmap decisions are reflected through reference architectures and design standards.

- Ensure technology adoption decisions align with long-term platform goals, deployment realities, and business outcomes.

- Serve as the primary product leader responsible for connecting innovation activity with scalable product development.

Regional Partnership & Deployment Enablement

- Establish a product deployment framework for energy systems aligned to Vantage’s product operating model.

- Partner closely with regional energy leaders across North America, EMEA, and APAC to ensure product strategies are deployable and aligned to market realities.

- Define global standards while enabling intentional regional flexibility where   required .

- Support Product Deployment teams in connecting energy products to specific customer and project opportunities.

- Identify   partnership opportunities that accelerate product capabilities and create market differentiation.

- Represent Vantage in strategic discussions related to energy infrastructure and future power systems.

- Support executive engagement with customers, regulators, and energy ecosystem partners.

Leadership Expectations

The Senior Director, Energy Systems is expected to   operate   as a strategic leader who influences outcomes across a highly matrixed global organization.

Success   requires :

- Strong systems thinking and strategic judgment with   an   ability to connect technology, infrastructure, commercial realities, and customer outcomes.

- Executive-level communication skills capable of influencing senior leadership and external stakeholders.

- A collaborative leadership style that builds alignment across Product Strategy, Product Engineering, Product Operations, Product Deployment, Regional Energy Teams, Delivery, Sustainability, Procurement, and Finance.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with utility interconnection studies and power procurement strategies.

- Knowledge of distributed energy resources, microgrids, energy storage systems, energy optimization, and grid services.

Energy is increasingly becoming the limiting factor for digital infrastructure growth. Vantage’s future success will depend on its ability to transform energy from a project-level constraint into a scalable   platform   capability.

The role requires substantive expertise in sustainability measurement methodologies, including GHG Protocol Scope 1–3, market-based and location-based Scope 2 accounting, 24/7 carbon-free energy accounting, water use effectiveness, and water accounting standards, combined with hands-on technical proficiency in SQL, Python or R, and BI platforms. Candidates should bring the methodological depth to make sound accounting judgments and the technical capability to operationalize them in scalable systems.

As a member of the Global Sustainability Center of Excellence, this role works closely with sustainability program owners and regional leads, and partners with IT, Investor Relations, Capital Markets, Corporate Development, Customer Experience, and Operations to ensure Sustainability data serves the full range of internal and external needs.

Essential Job Functions & Duties
Sustainability Data Architecture & Ecosystem Ownership

- Design and own the Sustainability data ecosystem, including how metrics are defined, sourced, calculated, validated, stored, and reused across all reporting, disclosure, and program management use cases.

- Establish and maintain a single source of truth for Sustainability metrics and calculation methodologies, with particular depth in GHG Protocol Scope 1, 2, and 3 accounting; market-based vs. location-based Scope 2 methodology selection and application; 24/7 carbon-free energy (CFE) accounting; water use effectiveness (WUE) and power usage effectiveness (PUE) metrics; and water accounting frameworks.

- Design structured, repeatable data flows that replace one-off data pulls to build the Sustainability data infrastructure that the organization and critical stakeholders can rely on as reporting obligations scale.

- Set and enforce standards for Sustainability data quality, definitions, documentation, timing, and traceability across all business units and geographies.

Systems, Platforms & Technical Data Infrastructure

- Own sustainability data and reporting platforms end‑to‑end, including workflow configuration, calculation logic, controls, platform governance, and evaluation of new tools as needs evolve.

- Design and maintain automated sustainability data pipelines using SQL and Python within a Microsoft‑based enterprise data environment (e.g., Azure data services, enterprise data lake/warehouse, Fabric or equivalent), reducing manual data handling and reconciliation.

- Develop curated sustainability datasets and semantic data models that enable consistent outputs across: Power BI dashboards, annual sustainability reporting, regulatory disclosures, and customer and investor data requests.

- Embed data lineage, metadata, audit trails, and explainability directly into sustainability data workflows so reported figures are defensible under third‑party assurance, internal audit, and executive review.

- Partner closely with IT and enterprise data teams to align sustainability data architecture with core data standards, security controls, and platform roadmaps, ensuring sustainability data is integrated into Vantage’s broader data ecosystem.

Customer & Investor Sustainability Data Solutions

- Develop and deliver customized Sustainability data packages and reporting solutions for customers and investors, including structured datasets, supporting methodology documentation, and responses to non-standard or contractually required disclosure requests.

- Serve as the Sustainability data point of contact for customer and investor reporting requests, assessing scope, determining the appropriate methodology, and ensuring outputs meet external quality and accuracy standards.

Data Collection & Reporting Execution

- Lead Sustainability data collection, preparation, validation, and quality assurance for the annual Sustainability Report, ensuring datasets are complete, audit-ready, and consistent with approved methodologies.

- Own the intake, scoping, and fulfillment of Sustainability reporting requests; distinguish between requests that can be addressed with existing data versus those requiring new collection or methodology development.

- Execute sustainability reporting and disclosure requests in partnership with the Sr. Manager, ensuring outputs meet established definitions, methodologies, and quality standards.

- Maintain a comprehensive reporting calendar and curate trusted, reusable datasets that reduce repetitive data work across disclosure cycles.

- Serve as the primary technical contact for third-party assurance providers and internal audit, defending data methodologies, calculation assumptions, and quality controls.

Program Enablement & Cross-Functional Partnership

- Act as the Sustainability data authority for sustainability program owners and regional leads, helping define data requirements for new initiatives and ensuring teams have reliable data to manage performance against targets.

- Train sustainability team members and data owners on how to access, interpret, and contribute to Sustainability data systems.

- Prepare structured Sustainability datasets and supporting materials to enable high-quality internal decision-making and external communications.

- Monitor the regulatory landscape for Sustainability disclosure requirements (e.g., CSRD/ESRS, ISSB, SEC climate rules, California SB 253 and 261) and proactively assess implications for Company's data systems and methodologies.

Job Requirements
Experience

- 7–10 years of experience in Sustainability reporting, sustainability analytics, environmental data management, or a combination of sustainability and data governance roles.

- Demonstrated experience designing or transforming structured Sustainability or environmental data collection and reporting processes in complex, multi-site organizations.

- Proven track record of moving a Sustainability or environmental reporting function from ad hoc, manual processes toward a standardized, system-driven operating model.

- Experience supporting Sustainability disclosures aligned with leading frameworks and regulations, with depth in at least two of: GHG Protocol, CSRD/ESRS, ISSB, SEC climate disclosure rules, SASB, TCFD, GRI.

- Experience preparing Sustainability data for third-party assurance, internal audit, or formal verification.

- Experience working in asset-intensive, operationally distributed, or capital-intensive organizations strongly preferred; data center, energy, or infrastructure experience is a differentiating advantage.

Sustainability Expertise (Required)

- Deep working knowledge of GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (Scope 1, 2, and 3), including the Scope 2 Guidance for market-based vs. location-based accounting and the practical application of instrument types (RECs, GOs, PPAs, VPPAs).

- Familiarity with 24/7 carbon-free energy (CFE) accounting frameworks

- Working knowledge of water accounting standards and metrics applicable to data center operations, including water use effectiveness (WUE), water consumption reporting and water risk assessment frameworks (e.g., WRI Aqueduct, AWS).

- Understanding of PUE (power usage effectiveness) as a data input for carbon and energy intensity calculations.

- Familiarity with nature-related disclosure frameworks (e.g., TNFD) is a plus.

Technical Skills (Required)

- Proficiency in SQL for querying, transforming, and validating large datasets across relational databases.

- Proficiency in Python for data manipulation, automation, and analytical workflows.

- Hands‑on experience developing dashboards, curated datasets, and analytical views in Power BI or comparable enterprise BI platforms.

- Hands-on experience with at least one enterprise Sustainability reporting platform (e.g., Workiva, Watershed, Persefoni, Sphera, or comparable) beyond basic data entry — including configuration, workflow design, and platform governance.

- Hands-on experience with Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) processes, data pipeline design, and automated workflow tools — sufficient to build simple pipelines independently and to partner credibly with IT on more complex data infrastructure.

- Strong data quality management skills, including the design and enforcement of validation rules, exception handling, and documentation standards.

Core Competencies

- Architectural thinking: ability to see how data flows across systems, processes, and stakeholders — and to redesign those flows for scale, accuracy, and auditability.

- Sound methodological judgment: ability to evaluate sustainability accounting methodologies, identify risks or gaps, and make and document defensible decisions.

- Cross-functional influence: demonstrated ability to align data owners, IT partners, and business stakeholders on data standards and delivery timelines without formal management authority.

- Clear communication: ability to explain Sustainability data concepts, methodology assumptions, and data limitations to both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Ownership and accountability: track record of owning work products and processes end-to-end, including through audit cycles.

- Equanimity under deadline pressure: ability to manage multiple competing priorities while maintaining quality and judgment during active reporting periods.

Education

- Bachelor's degree required in environmental science, data science, engineering, mathematics, statistics, accounting, or a related quantitative or environmental field. Master's degree or advanced certifications (e.g., GHG accounting, SASB FSA, CDMP) preferred.

Additional Details

title: Commissioning Program Developer, Global
description:
About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Product Department
The Product team at Vantage defines and stewards our global product platform: the customer outcomes we aim to deliver, the standards and reference approaches that make delivery repeatable, and the closed-loop learning that turns each deployment into an upgrade for the next. We do this in partnership with Engineering, Delivery, Operations, Procurement, Sustainability, Sales, Site Selection, and Business Development, aligning priorities and trade-offs while preserving clear functional ownership for design execution, construction delivery, commissioning, and site operations.

Position Overview
Vantage is building a repeatable, product-led approach to delivering and operating data centers at global scale. We are hiring a Commissioning Program Developer, Global to define and operate the global commissioning framework that makes that approach operationally real: the standards, requirements, methods, readiness gates, digital workflows, and feedback loops that turn commissioning from a project-specific activity into a scalable, repeatable capability.
This is a hands-on program development role for someone who combines deep commissioning and mission-critical delivery experience with the ability to build practical standards, influence cross-functional partners, and advance Commissioning as Code — translating repeatable commissioning logic, test procedures, evidence requirements, data structures, and reporting workflows into digital, automated, and scalable methods of execution.

What You Will Own
You will own the commissioning capability framework for our global product platform: the standards, requirements, methods, governance processes, digital workflows, and measures that make commissioning more repeatable, measurable, and scalable. Your work enables commissioning requirements to be embedded earlier in design, procurement, manufacturing, construction, and operational readiness, without taking project-level execution away from regional delivery teams.

What You Will Do

- Define and maintain global commissioning standards, requirements, methodologies, templates, readiness gates, and governance processes.

- Develop scalable commissioning approaches that can be consistently applied across regions, project types, and standardized infrastructure solutions.

- Translate business, customer, operational, engineering, and delivery requirements into practical commissioning strategies and execution frameworks.

- Partner with engineering, procurement, construction, manufacturing, supply chain, operations, automation, and regional delivery teams to embed commissioning requirements earlier in the project lifecycle.

- Develop strategies to move appropriate testing and validation activities upstream into factory, prefabrication, modular assembly, supplier, off-site, or near-site environments.

- Establish requirements for factory acceptance testing, supplier readiness, equipment validation, integrated system verification, and modular commissioning.

- Develop and advance Commissioning as Code by converting repeatable commissioning logic, procedures, checks, evidence requirements, and reporting needs into structured, digital, and where possible automated workflows.

- Partner with controls, automation, digital infrastructure, engineering, and operations teams to support automated testing, telemetry integration, data-driven validation, evidence management, and readiness reporting.

- Define commissioning data structures, reporting requirements, and analytics frameworks that support lessons learned, performance benchmarking, supplier quality insight, and long-term operational improvement.

- Provide training, implementation guidance, governance support, and adoption support for regional delivery and commissioning teams.

What Success Looks Like

- A global commissioning framework established, governed, and actively used across regions and project types.

- Commissioning requirements embedded earlier in the delivery lifecycle, with clear readiness gates before site execution risk materializes.

- Increased use of factory, supplier, off-site, near-site, and modular validation where appropriate.

- Commissioning as Code principles established, with repeatable procedures translated into structured workflows, data, automated checks, and traceable evidence capture.

- Reduced commissioning schedule risk, field labor intensity, rework, duplicated testing, and execution variability.

- Commissioning KPIs and reporting frameworks in place to measure readiness, quality, productivity, schedule impact, and continuous improvement.

- Lessons learned, commissioning data, supplier performance, and operational feedback captured and used to improve future standards and delivery methods.

What We Are Looking For

- 8+ years in commissioning, mission-critical infrastructure delivery, operational readiness, construction, engineering, manufacturing, automation, or related technical disciplines.

- Strong understanding of mechanical, electrical, controls, and integrated system commissioning principles in complex infrastructure environments.

- Experience developing commissioning standards, requirements, specifications, test procedures, readiness processes, or programmatic delivery frameworks.

- Experience leading cross-functional improvement initiatives across engineering, operations, construction, commissioning, procurement, suppliers, and regional delivery teams.

- Experience using data, metrics, lessons learned, and performance analysis to improve delivery outcomes.

- Clear written and executive communication that turns complexity into standards people will adopt.

- Ability to balance global consistency with regional delivery requirements, regulatory constraints, customer needs, and local execution realities.

Preferred

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, building systems, industrial engineering, controls, data center infrastructure, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent experience.

- Data center, mission-critical, advanced manufacturing, energy, technology infrastructure, or industrialized-delivery domain experience.

- Experience supporting modular, prefabricated, standardized, or manufacturing-based delivery models.

- Experience with factory acceptance testing, supplier quality processes, integrated systems validation, or off-site commissioning approaches.

- Working knowledge of controls systems, building automation systems, telemetry platforms, digital twins, commissioning software (for example CxAlloy), or data acquisition tools.

- Experience developing automated workflows, digital test procedures, structured evidence capture, data-driven validation, or software-enabled commissioning methods.

- Experience with high-density or AI-ready technical environments.

This role can be based in Ashburn, VA or remote.
In a Senior Director of Procurement Execution, NA Vantage is looking for an experienced, highly motivated, self-starter to be an integral part of a team that manages Owner Furnished Contractor Installed Equipment (OFCI) and corresponding supply chains.  In this role, you will lead and develop every aspect of the equipment procurement and delivery process from start to finish as well as lead other project managers. Daily responsibilities include providing executive leadership for North American Energy Procurement, Logistics, OFCI, and strategic sourcing functions; leading complex commercial negotiations and supplier partnerships; directing RFP development and contract execution; overseeing equipment procurement, submittals, and delivery performance; managing and forecasting capital budgets exceeding $800M; evaluating data center infrastructure strategies; and driving cross-functional alignment with Operations, Construction, Finance, Engineering, and executive leadership to ensure successful project execution, cost optimization, and supply chain resiliency.
As a Senior Director, you will be required to manage numerous projects in multiple regions simultaneously. Monthly travel to manufacturers and project sites will also be required.

Logistics, Inventory & Supply Chain Management

- Lead cross-functional teams responsible for transportation, warehousing, inventory planning, equipment allocation, and material flow across a multi-billion-dollar capital project portfolio.

- Develop and maintain multi-year inventory and capacity planning strategies, ensuring the availability of critical equipment while optimizing working capital, storage costs, and supply chain resiliency.

- Direct the development and execution of sourcing strategies, RFP processes, and commercial frameworks while providing guidance and executive support for complex supplier negotiations, contract execution, and risk management initiatives.

Market Development Department

The team collaborates with Commercial Management, Sales, Solution Engineering, Design Engineering, Construction, Operations, Finance, and Senior Management along the way. We also help ensure optimal revenue realization post-construction through development of commercial constructs and pricing that aligns to the objectives of both Vantage and our customers.

Position Overview
This role can be based in any of our US locations: Denver, CO; Phoenix, AZ; Santa Clara, CA; or Ashburn, VA.
The Vice President, Preconstruction is responsible for leading the strategic planning, design integration, and execution readiness of Vantage’s hyperscale and AI-driven data center developments. This role drives the full preconstruction lifecycle—from site validation and power feasibility through design development and transition to construction—ensuring projects are optimized for large-scale deployment, accelerated delivery, and high-density performance.
Grounded in Vantage’s core values of trust, integrity, accountability, teamwork, responsibility, and agility, the VP, Preconstruction serves as a critical connector across development, design, and construction. This leader ensures projects are fully de-risked, power-aligned, and scalable to support multi-phase campus builds and next-generation AI workloads, enabling confident investment decisions and predictable execution across a rapidly expanding portfolio.

Essential Job Functions

- Define and lead preconstruction strategy, standards, and scalable delivery models to support hyperscale and AI deployments. Establish repeatable processes that enable rapid campus expansion, multi-phase development, and speed-to-market execution. Align preconstruction priorities with power-first development strategy and customer-driven capacity needs.

- Lead comprehensive due diligence efforts with a strong emphasis on power availability, utility coordination, and long-term scalability. Oversee environmental, zoning, and permitting processes to ensure sites are entitled and executable at scale. Validate sites for large contiguous power capacity, phased expansion capability, and high-density infrastructure readiness.

- Lead early-stage design coordination, including campus master planning, high-density layouts, and basis-of-design development. Ensure alignment of design solutions with hyperscale and AI requirements, including liquid cooling readiness, high rack densities, and flexible infrastructure design. Drive integration between internal stakeholders and external partners to deliver efficient, scalable, and future-ready designs.

- Establish disciplined cost models and schedules that support rapid delivery timelines and phased capacity deployment. Drive decision-making that balances cost, speed, and scalability while maintaining transparency and financial rigor. Identify risks early and implement mitigation strategies to protect delivery certainty in power-constrained or fast-moving markets.

- Ensure seamless project handoff with fully defined scope, aligned budgets, and construction-ready documentation. Enable construction teams to execute quickly by delivering well-defined, de-risked, and permit-ready projects. Maintain continuity and accountability through strong partnership with construction leadership.

- Partner with real estate, development, design, construction, operations, and commercial teams to ensure alignment with enterprise growth objectives. Support customer engagement by aligning preconstruction solutions with hyperscale and AI workload requirements. Drive enterprise-first decision-making that prioritizes portfolio scale, repeatability, and operational excellence.

- Champion new design strategies, delivery methods, and technologies that enhance density, efficiency, and deployment speed. Continuously improve preconstruction processes based on lessons learned across the portfolio and evolving AI infrastructure demands.

- Represent Vantage with utilities, jurisdictions, and strategic partners to secure power, entitlements, and project approvals. Build trusted relationships that accelerate timelines and position Vantage as a preferred partner in key hyperscale markets.

- Additional duties as assigned by Management

- Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Real Estate, or related field; advanced degree preferred.

- 15+ years of experience in preconstruction, development, design, or construction leadership within data centers, infrastructure, or large-scale industrial projects.

- Proven experience delivering hyperscale or campus-style developments, including multi-phase project execution.

- Deep expertise in power-driven site selection, due diligence, design management, and cost estimation.

- Experience supporting projects with high-density compute environments and evolving AI infrastructure requirements preferred.

The successful candidate will be confident writing queries and developing tables, program views, functions, and stored procedures. Site Operations Department
The Site Operations Department is responsible for the overall health of all mechanical and electrical systems, building maintenance, and performance of all data modules in our data centers. The team is staffed 24 x 7 onsite with Critical Facility Engineers (CFEs) on each shift.
This team is the face of Vantage to our customers and the first line of defense regarding the uptime of our campus as well as the performance of our customer installations. Using a Critical Maintenance Management System (CMMS) to plan and track work needed, the Site Operations department performs all preventative and corrective maintenance. Our culture expects and rewards team performance that engages directly with the customers and the facility infrastructure. This is a team that does most of the actual work versus calling upon vendors. As a result, we provide superior service that is faster and more cost effective.

Position Overview
This role is onsite in Ashburn, VA. This is an in-house position.

Ideally we will be seeking experienced talent for Levels I or potentially II . One with data center, mission critical field service or mission critical military experience highly desired (US Navy, US Air Force, US Army, US Marines, US Coast Guard). These are in-house and hands-on roles using your critical thinking talents to troubleshoot and fix equipment vs subbing out the work.

Electrical and mechanical expertise in a non-mission critical field service in cross-industry may be considered, e.g, chiller technician with larger tonnage but non-critical environments or field service in OEM equipment outside of data center. (Johnson Controls, York, Trane, Daikin, Vertiv, Eaton, Liebert, Toshiba, Delta, CAT, ABB, Samsung, Mitsubishi, Siemens, Petra etc) . We are also able to consider those that are very trainable.

We are looking for a Critical Facilities Engineer who knows what best-in-class service looks like and can make that a reality.  This role is an important member of our facilities team where we manage some of the most efficient and cost-effective data center facilities in the industry.

The successful candidate for this role will work with a team of other electrical and mechanical-focused engineers performing maintenance and repair for our data center infrastructure.  We take our customer requirements for uptime seriously and keep our facilities maintained to a very high standard to insure uninterrupted service for our customers.

If you enjoy working on critical data center systems (UPSs, PDUs, Diesel Generators, ATS equipment and Building Controls), as well as industrial electrical equipment and systems that include power distribution components/wiring, electronic components and lighting systems.  If you know the importance of getting it right the first time and not disrupting mission critical data centers.  If you enjoy delighting customers with superior service and you have the desire and ability to do so, then please read on!

- Manage multiple one-time and/or ongoing projects

- Respond to safety and emergency situations and maintain a safe and secure work environment

- Use discretion and judgment in organizing workflow and adapting as priorities are modified due to a changing environment

- Frequent contact with employees at all levels of the organization; frequent external contact with vendors

Duties

- Develop reliability reports to ensure availability and capacity targets are achieved and maintained with 100% uptime

- Coordinate, and oversee all maintenance vendors to ensure personnel safety, protect the Facility’s critical equipment, and maintain power to the critical load

- Create required MOPs (Method of Procedure), SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) and EOPs (Emergency Operating Procedures) to ensure all maintenance activities are performed in accordance to them

- Additional duties as assigned by Management

- Demonstrate knowledge in operating, maintaining, repairing, inspecting and testing critical electrical distribution systems, HVAC systems and building management/automation equipment

- Ability to read commercial building blueprints and understand electrical single lines and schematics

- Knowledge of commonly-used concepts, practices, and procedures related to mechanical & electrical systems needed to run data centers

We are creating a new senior leadership role to build and lead Vantage’s fleetwide reliability and technical assurance capability. The function provides a stronger central mechanism for understanding reliability risk, validating critical controls, learning from incidents, and converting those lessons into durable improvements across the operating fleet. Its purpose is to set, govern, and assure global operations standards, performance, and risk across the portfolio.

The function owns portfolio-wide operational standards, governance, performance visibility, and operational risk. It provides a common framework for measuring operational performance, identifying systemic risks and trends, and driving consistency, accountability, and continuous improvement across regions while preserving regional ownership of day-to-day operations.

The role complements regional Operations and Reliability Engineering teams, who remain accountable for live site operations, incident command, maintenance, and customer operational delivery. It provides central assurance, expert challenge, practical support, cross-region learning, and a structured route to escalate systemic risks and investment needs to the Executive Leadership Team.

The orienting lens is customer impact. Across a large and varied operating fleet, the function applies proportionate, risk-based assurance — concentrating effort where customer commitments and operating reputation are most material, rather than uniformly across technical risk.

This is a build mandate. The successful candidate will shape the function from the ground up with executive sponsorship, formal authority within its remit, owned budget for a focused direct team, and direct visibility to the Executive Leadership Team.

This role will ideally be based in Denver, Colorado or London, England.

Essential Job Functions

Establish the fleetwide reliability baseline and risk model. Build the common reliability and resilience baseline. Define a risk-ranking method that leads with customer-impacting risk. Stand up the recurring assurance cycle and the evidence model for critical controls.

Lead technical assurance, inspection, and critical control verification. Lead high-consequence independent reviews and field verification across electrical, mechanical, controls, automation, emergency response, and commissioning.

Drive corrective action and closed-loop learning. Translate incidents, near misses, and weak signals into structured learning. Maintain a risk-ranked corrective action register. Ensure validated lessons feed into the standards, procedures, telemetry, supplier requirements, training, and capital plans that apply across the fleet.

Foster transparent reporting and accountable learning. Build an environment in which honest errors, near misses, and weak signals are surfaced early, and frontline teams are treated as a primary source of operational intelligence.

Develop the roadmap for configuration and automation drift detection. Partner with Product, Automation, IT, and Cybersecurity on requirements for telemetry, alarm quality, configuration management, and AI-enabled drift detection. As capability matures, AI-enabled tooling may help identify anomalies, drift, and candidate corrective actions for review.

Establish executive reporting and governance. Set the operating cadence with Operations. Prepare concise monthly executive reporting that drives decisions, not reporting theater. Provide portfolio-level visibility into operational performance, risk, and trends through standardized metrics and reporting frameworks. Distinguish site execution issues from systemic patterns, standards gaps, supplier issues, and investment constraints.

Set and govern global operational standards, performance, and risk. Own the global operational standards framework and associated policies. Establish portfolio-wide KPIs, metrics, and reporting frameworks that provide clear visibility into operational performance, reliability risk, and emerging trends. Roll up fleetwide performance and risk into executive-level insights that distinguish local execution issues from systemic patterns. Audit compliance with standards, identify systemic gaps and portfolio-wide improvement opportunities, and drive consistency, governance, accountability, and continuous improvement across regions.

Build and lead the function. Hold owned budget and the authority to build a focused direct team, operating through a wider cross-functional assurance network rather than a parallel organization. Exercise formal authority within the remit — require evidence, set assurance scope and cadence, conduct reviews and inspections, own the central corrective action register, require management responses, and require deviations from critical controls to be explicit, risk-ranked, time-bound, approved, and visible — escalating findings directly to the Executive Leadership Team, in partnership with regional teams.

Additional Duties as assigned by Management.

Job Requirements
• 15+ years in mission-critical operations, reliability engineering, operational assurance, critical facilities, industrial operations, process safety, or another high-reliability environment.
• Demonstrated experience leading reliability, technical assurance, operational excellence, engineering assurance, or risk-based inspection across a complex operating fleet.
• Strong working understanding of mission-critical electrical, mechanical, controls, automation, commissioning, maintenance, and operating procedure environments.
• Experience investigating incidents, near misses, recurring defects, or systemic reliability issues and converting findings into practical corrective actions.
• Experience building governance or assurance systems that drive operational improvement rather than reporting alone.
• Credible field presence: comfortable with site walks, control rooms, methods of procedure, maintenance realities, and difficult technical conversations — not solely an executive-reporting leader.
• The ability to operate through influence in a matrixed environment, with the credibility to challenge senior regional, operations, engineering, and technical leaders while maintaining trust and partnership.
• Executive-level communication: concise risk narratives, decision-ready papers, and credibility with a senior executive audience.
• Global Travel required is expected to be up to 30%-40% but may increase over time as the business evolves.

Preferred
• Hyperscale data center or colocation operations experience.
• Experience in adjacent high-reliability sectors — utilities, power generation, aviation, semiconductor manufacturing, oil and gas, nuclear, pharmaceuticals, or advanced manufacturing.
• Familiarity with operational technology, BMS and SCADA, alarm quality, configuration management, and telemetry.
• Experience building or scaling a new function in a high-growth environment.
• Professional engineering qualification or equivalent technical credibility.

Why This Matters
This is an unusual platform: a function created from the ground up, with executive sponsorship, formal authority within its remit, and direct impact on customer outcomes and operating reputation. The role will establish the operating system that governs standards, performance visibility, and operational risk across a rapidly growing global portfolio, reinforcing Vantage’s values of trust, accountability, respect, and agility.

Physical Demands and Special Requirements

Automation Systems Group
The Automation Systems Group is responsible for the design, construction and support of cutting-edge data center automation and control infrastructure. Automation Systems works closely with partner contractors to come up with the best design and helps manage these partners to success by providing accurate requirements, goals, and timelines. This role can be based in Phoenix, AZ; Denver, CO; New Albany, OH; Ashburn, VA; Atlanta, GA; San Antonio, TX or Abilene TX, following Vantage's hybrid work policy (3 days in the office; 2 days flexible).

Vantage is looking for a motivated, detail-oriented, hands-on Senior Automation Telemetry Engineer to support telemetry systems development, customer usage tracking, operational data delivery, and internal data needs across Vantage facilities.

title: Sr. Platform Owner, Halo, Global
description:
About Vantage

Information Technology Department
The Information Technology Department architects and operates the digital foundation powering Vantage global operations while pioneering the intelligent transformation of how we work. Our integrated IT/AI organization delivers enterprise-grade infrastructure, networking, cybersecurity, and end-user services with operational excellence, while simultaneously developing artificial intelligence capabilities that drive measurable business value. We are transforming our service delivery model around ITIL best practices, comprehensive automation frameworks, and governance structures that enable both stability and innovation. Our teams collaborate across Infrastructure, Network, Service Desk, IT Engineering, and Artificial Intelligence functions, emphasizing service over technology and recognizing that success is measured by business outcomes rather than technical implementations. This is an exceptional time to join as we fundamentally reshape how technology serves the organization, creating an environment where operational discipline and innovative experimentation work as complementary forces.

Artificial Intelligence Team
The Artificial Intelligence Team exists to amplify human potential through intelligent technology. We're building an AI-powered ecosystem that transforms how Vantage creates value, freeing our people from routine work so they can focus on innovation and strategic thinking that truly differentiates us in the market. Through responsible AI implementation across operations, engineering, and business functions, we're not just automating processes; we're reimagining what's possible when human creativity partners with artificial intelligence. Our approach centers on measurable business outcomes, ethical governance, and creating capabilities that make every team member more effective while positioning Vantage at the forefront of the intelligent infrastructure revolution.

Position Overview

This position will be based remotely in the United States.

The Sr. Platform Owner, Halo, Global is the technical and strategic owner of Vantage’s Halo AI platform, responsible for ensuring the platform’s health, scalability, security, and continuous evolution as the backbone for custom AI solutions and intelligent applications across the enterprise. While Copilot serves Microsoft 365 productivity workflows, Halo is Vantage’s purpose-built platform for deploying custom AI applications, agentic workflows, and intelligent automation solutions that address industry-specific challenges. This role combines deep technical expertise in cloud AI infrastructure, application platforms, and enterprise architecture with product ownership discipline, managing the platform lifecycle from architecture design through production operations. Success requires balancing platform robustness with development velocity, ensuring the Accelerators team has a reliable foundation for rapid prototyping while custom solutions meet enterprise production standards for security, performance, and scalability.

Essential Job Functions

- Own the end-to-end health, performance, and reliability of the Halo platform, establishing monitoring frameworks, SLAs, and operational procedures that ensure platform availability and performance meet enterprise standards.

- Define and execute the Halo platform roadmap, balancing infrastructure stability with capability expansion based on Accelerators team needs, Navigator opportunity insights, and emerging AI technology capabilities.

- Architect and maintain the Halo platform infrastructure including compute resources, AI model hosting, data pipelines, API gateways, and integration frameworks that enable rapid development and reliable production operations.

- Establish development standards, deployment patterns, and integration templates that enable the Accelerators team to build and deploy solutions efficiently while maintaining platform architectural integrity.

- Manage Halo security controls, data governance policies, and compliance frameworks that protect organizational data and meet enterprise security requirements for AI application deployment.

- Collaborate with IT and Security teams on platform infrastructure including cloud architecture, network security, identity management, and monitoring that aligns Halo with enterprise technology standards.

- Evaluate and integrate emerging AI technologies, frameworks, and services into the Halo platform, maintaining a modern technology stack that supports the organization’s evolving AI capabilities.

- Develop technical documentation, architecture decision records, and developer guides that enable efficient onboarding and reduce platform team dependencies.

Duties

- Monitor Halo platform health across all layers including infrastructure, application services, AI model performance, API availability, and integration endpoints, investigating and resolving issues proactively.

- Manage cloud infrastructure for Halo including Azure resource optimization, cost management, capacity planning, and scaling strategies that balance performance with financial efficiency.

- Design and implement CI/CD pipelines, deployment automation, and environment management that enable rapid prototyping cycles while maintaining production stability.

- Configure and maintain security controls including authentication/authorization frameworks, API key management, data encryption, network segmentation, and audit logging for all Halo components.

- Create and maintain developer toolkits, starter templates, and SDK components that accelerate solution development on the Halo platform while ensuring architectural consistency.

- Conduct platform architecture reviews for solutions built by the Accelerators team, ensuring custom applications align with Halo standards and can transition smoothly to production.

- Manage platform vendor relationships including Azure service agreements, AI model provider contracts, and third-party component licenses that support Halo capabilities.

- Design and execute platform load testing, security assessments, and disaster recovery exercises that validate Halo readiness for enterprise-scale operations.

- Troubleshoot complex platform issues spanning infrastructure, application, and AI model layers, coordinating with cloud providers and technology partners when needed.

- Support the Platform Owner, Halo in day-to-day platform operations, mentoring and guiding their development while ensuring consistent quality across platform management activities.

- Participate in technology evaluation and proof-of-concept development for emerging AI frameworks, model architectures, and infrastructure capabilities that could enhance Halo.

- Handle additional duties as assigned by Management.

Job Requirements

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field required; Azure certifications (AZ-104, AZ-305, AI-102) or equivalent cloud platform certifications strongly preferred.

- Experience leading or managing AI programs, platforms, or technology initiatives in enterprise environments.

- Extensive experience building, operating, and scaling cloud-based application platforms, with demonstrated expertise in Azure services including App Services, Functions, Container Apps, AI Services, and infrastructure management.

- Deep technical knowledge of AI/ML deployment infrastructure, including model hosting, inference optimization, vector databases, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architectures, and agentic framework deployment.

- Strong software engineering background with proficiency in Python and TypeScript/JavaScript, as well as modern development practices including CI/CD, infrastructure as code, containerization, and API design. Demonstrated enthusiasm for leveraging AI-powered development tools to accelerate agentic solution development.

- Experience with enterprise security architecture, including identity and access management (Azure AD/Entra ID), network security, data encryption, and compliance controls for cloud-native applications.

- Practical knowledge of AI frameworks and technologies including LangChain, Semantic Kernel, Azure OpenAI, and conversational AI platforms, with an understanding of their integration within enterprise platform architectures.

- Demonstrated success managing complex platform lifecycles, including capacity planning, release management, incident response, and technical debt reduction within production environments.

- Strong architectural and strategic thinking skills, with experience evaluating technology trade-offs, making build-versus-buy decisions, and designing scalable platforms that balance current business needs with future flexibility.

- Experience optimizing developer experience (DevEx) through documentation, tooling, templates, automation, and support processes that improve engineering productivity and solution delivery velocity.

- Excellent problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose and resolve complex issues across infrastructure, application, and AI model layers in distributed cloud environments.

- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to articulate platform architecture, technical constraints, and strategic recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Self-directed and proactive, with a demonstrated ability to identify, prioritize, and address emerging technical challenges before they impact users or platform performance.

About Vantage

Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Site Operations Department
The Site Operations Department is responsible for the overall health of all mechanical and electrical systems, building maintenance, and performance of all data modules in our data centers. The team is staffed 24 x 7 onsite with Critical Facilities Engineers (CFEs) working on shift and reporting to a Chief Engineer. This team is the face of Vantage to our customers and the guarantee of business continuity and excellence of Operations of our campus as well as the performance of our customer installations. Using a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) to plan and track maintenance activities, the Site Operations Department is responsible for all preventative and corrective maintenance. Our culture expects and rewards team performance that engages directly with the customers and the facility infrastructure.

Position Overview

The successful candidate for this Critical Facilities Technician role knows what best-in-class data center service looks like and can make that a reality.  This role is an important member of our Operations team where we manage some of the most efficient and cost-effective data center facilities in the industry.
Persons this role will work with a team of other electrical and mechanical-focused engineers performing maintenance and repair for our data center infrastructure.  We take our customer requirements for uptime seriously and keep our facilities maintained to a very high standard to insure uninterrupted service for our customers.
If you enjoy working on critical data center systems (UPSs, PDUs, Diesel Generators, ATS equipment, and Building Controls), as well as industrial electrical equipment and systems that include power distribution components/wiring, electronic components, and lighting systems.  If you know the importance of getting it right the first time and not disrupting mission-critical data centers.  If you enjoy delighting customers with superior service and you have the desire and ability to do so, then please read on!
Essential Job Functions

- Operate, monitor, maintain, and respond to abnormal conditions in facility systems. Areas includes: Electrical, mechanical, building monitoring, and control

- Ensure the completion of maintenance activities to the highest quality level of planification, preparation, execution, and reporting

- Ensure the full reliability of the infrastructures with the focus on continuity of services and energy efficiency

- Use the BMS (Building Management System) and all available systems to appropriate monitoring the site including regular walkthroughs verifying the good working condition

Duties

- Work in shifts, per assigned shift pattern and wear personal protecting clothes depending on the work to be performed

- Within applicable and authorized interventions according to the local regulation and the up-to-date certification(s) of the Critical Facilities Technician, be capable of manipulating / activating certain electrical and or mechanical and or security infrastructures for the purpose of protecting people and property and / or maintaining service continuity on the site

- Use of the Building Management System (BMS) and regular onsite checks

- With the assistance of the IT and Controls departments, ensure the proper operation of the site BMS

- In close collaboration with the contractors, participate in the drafting of the preventive maintenance schedule for the site infrastructures and implement it in collaboration with all service providers concerned. Closely monitor the operations with a continuous concern for minimizing risks during interventions, and ensure the reporting of this activity

- Operational management of suppliers and service providers, to document and plan preventive maintenance and or repair activities. Using a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) and the Change Management Process.

- Closely monitor the work of vendors with a continuous concern for minimizing risks during interventions, ensuring cleanliness standard, and ensure proper reporting of the performed activity

- Perform repair and maintenance activities as required

- Implementation of improvement plans and small projects

- Participate in the implementation of the site-specific crisis management plan and in the tests and implementation exercises concerning this plan

- Participate in regular site audits and reviews, which are designed to assess the level of service continuity and analyze risks

Job Requirements

- Technical education (advanced technician or engineer level) in one of the following areas: Electricity (generators, UPS, low voltage distribution), climate, and cooling.

- Experience in operating data centers or similar environments

- Versatile technical knowledge, especially in the areas of operation, maintenance, and inspection of critical systems

- English language – The minimum level required is B1 (intermediate, able to understand and communicate about familiar topics and handle most everyday situations independently)

- Knowledge of fire protection and physical security (access control, video, and intrusion detection systems) or central building management systems is advantageous.

- Good communication skills with third parties and internal customers

- Highly motivated at problem-solving

- Attention to detail and a genuine commitment to following up on actions

- Good writing skills

- Everyday use of standard office equipment

- Proven skills in the use of software, such as BMS, Computerized Maintenance Management Systems

- Potential employees must complete a background check successfully

Physical activities and requirements

- Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, poles and the like

- Raising objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position-to-position.

- Raised floor work.  Must be able to maneuver and work underneath and around raised floor of varying heights.

Reliability Engineering
The Reliability Engineering Department is responsible for ensuring the operational health of critical systems and the implementation of Site Operations best practices. This includes evaluating the performance and reliability of critical infrastructure, maintaining operational availability through maintenance programs, and providing technical support to Site Operations teams. The department also collaborates closely with the Design Engineering team to provide feedback for future data center designs.

Position Overview
This role will be based near any of our North America office locations, following our flexible work policy (3 days in-office and 2 days flexible).
The Sr. Technical Project Manager, Site Deployment - Mechanical Design Assurance is responsible for providing operationally focused mechanical review and technical assurance for new data center builds, expansions, and major fit-out projects across the North America portfolio. This role represents Site Operations and Site Deployment during design development, page-turn reviews, submittal reviews, RFI responses, commissioning strategy alignment, and movement of design packages toward Issued for Construction drawings.
The position ensures that mechanical systems are designed and delivered in a manner that is operable, maintainable, safe, reliable, and aligned with long-term Mission Critical Operations requirements. Working closely with Design Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Business Operations, and local Site Operations teams, this role brings operator perspective into design decisions before construction execution, procurement, and turnover activities create downstream operational risk.

- Provide operator perspective on sequence of operations, controls strategy, sensor placement, alarm strategy, setpoints, trending capability, and emergency operating scenarios.

- Review proposed equipment substitutions or manufacturer deviations for potential impacts to maintainability, spare parts, training, warranty, resilience, and operational standardization.

- Support development of operational design standards, mechanical review checklists, lessons learned repositories, and acceptance criteria used by the Site Deployment organization.

- Partner with local MCO leadership to ensure future operators understand mechanical design intent, operating limitations, maintenance requirements, and known risk items prior to turnover.

Job Requirements

- 5+ years of experience in data center operations, mechanical engineering, commissioning, critical facilities maintenance, construction QA/QC, or mission-critical infrastructure delivery.

- Strong working knowledge of data center mechanical systems, including chilled water, airside cooling, pumping systems, mechanical controls, water treatment, and supporting utility systems.

- Experience reviewing mechanical drawings, specifications, submittals, commissioning documents, sequence of operations, and technical vendor documentation.

- Ability to identify operability, maintainability, reliability, safety, and lifecycle risks within mechanical design packages before construction execution.

- Strong communication skills with the ability to clearly articulate operator concerns to Design Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, and Site Operations stakeholders.

- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent projects, track comments and issues to closure, and support fixed project milestones.

- Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and familiarity with project documentation, drawing management, and issue tracking workflows.

Job Requirements

This position will be based on-site at our office in Denver, CO. in alignmen t with our flexible work policy. (3 days on site required, 2 days flexible).

Vantage Data Centers is seeking a Sr Data Engineer to help build, operate, and scale the governed data foundation for Operations, North America. This role is designed for an engineer who can independently deliver production-ready pipelines, curated datasets, semantic-model inputs, and AI-ready data products that support reporting, Executive reporting insight preparation, and the emerging AI Insight Solution.
As part of the Data Engineering & Business Intelligence team, you will be responsible for delivering reliable data products that support analytics, AI data agents, operational intelligence, reporting, and an emerging AI-enabled platform. You will work closely with IT Global, solution build teams, business SMEs, and data governance partners to ensure data products are secure, reusable, explainable, and aligned with enterprise AI / Fabric direction.
Success in this position requires comfort with ambiguity, strong execution discipline, and accountability for building trusted data assets that can be reused across analytics, operational intelligence, and AI-enabled use cases.

Essential Job Functions

- Design, build, and maintain reliable, scalable data pipelines using Python and PySpark on the Microsoft Azure data platform.

- Develop and operate batch and incremental data pipelines leveraging Azure Data Factory for orchestration and Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 as the primary data store.

- Build and maintain curated lakehouse / gold-layer datasets and semantic-model inputs that support governed operational insights and AI-enabled consumption.

- Independently implement SQL- and Spark-based transformations to produce curated datasets that support enterprise reporting, analytics, AI-enabled insight preparation, and downstream consumption.

- Take ownership of assigned data pipelines and datasets, including monitoring, troubleshooting, performance optimization, documentation, and production support.

- Work with Azure Synapse, Microsoft Fabric / Lakehouse patterns where applicable, and related Azure analytics services to support analytical workloads and data consumption patterns.

- Prepare structured operational data for AI-enabled use cases by documenting business rules, source lineage, data reliability constraints, known quality limitations, and data dictionary definitions.

- Support source visibility, confidence context, and Data Reliability & Trust Indicator integration where applicable so downstream analytics and AI outputs can be understood and trusted.

- Contribute to ontology, taxonomy, semantic model, and data dictionary alignment needed to connect operational context, KPIs, incidents, work orders, and other enterprise data domains.

- Collaborate with business analysts, operations SMEs, data stewards, IT Global, and cross-functional stakeholders to translate requirements into practical, working data solutions.

- Apply established data governance, security, access-control, data classification, and engineering standards to ensure compliant, maintainable, and scalable solutions.

- Identify, document, and route data-quality issues to accountable owners, helping improve source correction rather than masking defects downstream.

- Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, sprint planning, and platform improvement initiatives as an active contributor.

- Proactively identify data quality issues, pipeline risks, platform dependencies, and improvement opportunities, and communicate them clearly in a fast-paced environment.

Duties

- Develop and maintain PySpark notebooks and jobs to ingest, transform, validate, and curate data within the enterprise data platform.

- Build and modify Azure Data Factory pipelines for batch and incremental data ingestion.

- Implement Spark-based transformations that write curated datasets to Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 and/or Fabric Lakehouse patterns using established folder structures, naming conventions, and governance standards.

description:
About Vantage Data Centers

Vantage Data Centers powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Position Overview

Vantage is looking for a Director, Project Controls, to support project controls functions as part of our end to-end data center development cycle. As a leader, you will drive a company program supporting four main pillars within project controls including scheduling, cost estimating, change management and reporting.
You will be charged with building and leading a great team and leveraging internal and external resources to enable delivery teams to improve speed to market, drive to optimized returns through lower build costs, help manage/mitigate risks, and have a repeatable/scalable change management process.

Essential Job Functions

- Provide overall leadership to architect and improve project controls system, processes and specifications to enable teams to leverage historical data, leverage predictive analytics, and support data-driven decision making.

- Collaborate with Innovation Engineering, Site Selection/New Site Development, and Construction teams to provide end-to-end support and feedback loop to tie actuals to future improvements.

- Oversee the production of project schedules throughout project lifecycle to support internal and external development teams to meet or exceed targets.

- Cost Management:

- Establish useable budgets and manage costs to meet or exceed cost targets.

- Leverage cost databases using Vantage software programs to establish budget accuracy and optimize financial results.

- Utilize cost accounting software dashboards with real-time telemetry at project, site, region, and national levels.

- Contribute to the month-end financial forecasting process and ensure risk exposure and gainful opportunities are accurately reported

- Risk and Change Management:

- At project start, develop risk management plans and maintain them throughout the project with mitigation strategies.

- Establish a change management workflow incorporating existing processes and best practices.

- Support Development design and Operations evaluations to assess cost and schedule impacts of proposed changes.

- Performance Monitoring and Reporting:

- Utilize data to produce real-time status, KPIs, and predictive analytics.

- Prepare detailed cost, schedule, risk, and upside reports for project teams and management.

- Contribute to the month-end financial forecasting process and ensure risk exposure is accurately reported.

- Programmatic Support

- Create and maintain schedule database to set allowable ranges of each activity based real data; leverage cost database to do the same.

- Leverage data to produce real-time status, KPIs and predictive analytics systems.

- Propagate use of standard breakdown structures (WBS, CBS, etc.) and Schedule of Values (SOV) to ensure consistent data capture and accurate cross-referencing of budgets and actuals.

- Maintain program level schedule updates, prepare site specific schedules, and cost/schedule customer deliverables.

- Leverage leading and lagging indicators to help project teams identify impacts proactively and support development of mitigation plans

- Reporting

- Develop dashboards with real-time telemetry at project, site, region and global levels; deliver detailed cost, schedule, risk/upside reports for the project teams and management as needed.

- Contribute to the month-end financial forecasting process.

- Ensure risk exposure is accurately extracted from the Risk/Upside Log into other reports.

- Provide project teams with schedule lookahead metrics o Run analyses to compare the work in place to the progress billings to report risk to budget or schedule.

- Development Projects (Preconstruction and Construction)

- Support time-impact analysis throughout development stage gates.

- Ensure contractors comply with cost/schedule formats and data inputs enabling efficient data management.

- Work with project teams and Construction Cost and Finance (CCF) to improve project estimating process at each development stage including conceptual design, SD, DD, CD

- Partner with CCF to establish cost standardization, benchmarking, labor analysis/efficiency and forecasting/ variance analysis to identify risks as well as opportunities to optimize ongoing and future builds.

- Support project teams in the development of Schedule of Values

- Review and perform health check analysis on contractor’s baseline and progress schedules.

- Additional duties as assigned by Management

- Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering, Quantity Surveying or certification as Project Controls Manager or equivalent required, MBA is helpful.

- 8 years of experience in project controls management required 10 to 12 years preferred

- Global construction experience is required, and data Center experience is strongly preferred, but not required.

- Understanding general project controls technical skills and the integration of all of the components including organizational, planning, accounting, analysis and revision process areas.

- Experience in P6 software and interface with accounting software like Yardi and Anaplan strongly preferred.

- Strong organizational and time management skills

- Strong analytical and interpersonal skills
